articles.title: IPL media rights: Industry seeks best price-discovery models
articles.summary: Cricket News: Last week, the ICC sounded the media-rights bugle by appointing a five-member working group. The group’s top priority in the coming months will be to .
articles.body: Last week, the ICC sounded the media-rights bugle by appointing a five-member working group. The group’s top priority in the coming months will be to consider all possible steps that can help the ICC retain the existing value for the 2028-31 cycle, or even better it, by exploring the best price-discovery models available. The ICC’s media-rights tender, however, will not be the first to hit the market. The world governing body will have to wait for the BCCI to first draft and release the IPL media-rights tender, following which any other property around the world, including the ICC, will come up for sale.Meanwhile, the BCCI is yet to act on it. The Indian cricket administration, usually considered a sleeping giant unless woken from its slumber, hasn’t taken a call yet on bringing a financial agency on board to figure out the right price-discovery models, as it did during the previous rights cycle. Interestingly, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia is on the ICC media rights working group, which ECB chief Richard Thompson is heading and also includes ICC chairman Jay Shah.In 2022, the cricket board brought in financial advisory firm KPMG to draft the IPL tender document. This document included a special non-exclusive digital-rights package designed for selling a select ‘bouquet’ of high-value matches in the Indian subcontinent. Set at 18 matches per season for a 74-game structure, this package alone rose to Rs 3,273 crore at Rs 33.24 crore per game and ensured Internet rights ended up generating more revenue for the BCCI from the subcontinent for the first time in history than the traditional sale of TV rights.“We were expecting to hear something from them (BCCI) on this. Given the way tech is changing how we consume sport, we thought the board would be keen to explore these changing revenue patterns and models for IPL. Look at the YouTube sports-bundling model in the US, for instance. The NFL Sunday Ticket is a case study in itself,” said an industry executive.Sports industry executives strongly believe that the value can be tremendous if the BCCI explores this space in greater detail. The BCCI members will be in Mumbai starting on Friday for the AGM. Those tracking developments can’t think of a more important subject the members may need to discuss than the upcoming sale of media rights.“India has a strong cricket platform. The IPL is already a premium property on that platform. All you need to build on it is effectively what can be done outside of the live match feed. Archives, highlights, documentaries, regional storytelling, fan engagement etc. You may have one or two broadcasters in the race for rights but building a separate non-live consumer base to monetise premium properties selectively is another subject matter altogether,” the executive added.The key aligning principle here must be based on a modular concept, rather than the all-inclusive one that currently prevails. “Perhaps not a very healthy model either, considering all your eggs happen to be in one single basket,” says an IPL franchise executive, referring to IPL’s heavy leaning on JioStar for live broadcasts. OTT giant Netflix hasn’t majorly dabbled with the idea of putting live sport behind its paywall. However, it has certainly not backed away from exploring events that can be included within its existing plans to create a reason for people to remain subscribed.“We keep wondering why an Amazon or a Netflix or a YouTube hasn’t looked at the India market. Well, the fact is, the onus lies on us to market our products to them and only then can we catch their attention. So, in the case of IPL rights, the onus certainly lies on the BCCI to go out and start talking to these platforms,” the franchise executive added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Clear message’ for Hardik Pandya: Gautam Gambhir reveals what the all-rounder must do to return to Team India
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through gam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through game time, with the all-rounder currently not part of India's squads after not playing enough cricket since the IPL.Following India's 127-run win over Afghanistan in the third T20I in New Delhi on Thursday, Gambhir said Pandya's immediate priority should be getting back on the field, including through the India A series, before pushing for a return to the senior sides."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs, and he hasn't played a lot of cricket since the IPL, so we don't want to push him into international cricket because international cricket can be extremely tough on your body as well," Gambhir said during the post-match press conference.The India head coach also revealed that the message to Pandya has been straightforward: play, regain match fitness and then push for a place in both white-ball squads."And that was the clear message to him that if he can play that India A series, and then if everything goes well, he can come back and be part of the T20s and the one-day squad as well," Gambhir said.India could play Hardik and Nitish togetherGambhir's comments also highlighted India's plans to develop more than one seam-bowling all-rounder. Nitish Kumar Reddy, initially included in India's 15-member Asian Games squad, has been withdrawn from the continental event and will instead feature in the ODI series against the West Indies.Gambhir believes the move will give Reddy valuable game time and accelerate his development with the ball ahead of India's future assignments."From Nitish's point of view, it's actually a great thing that he's been withdrawn from the T20 format, and he'll get game time against the West Indies as well," he said. "We know how important a seam-bowling all-rounder will probably be in a year and when we go to South Africa. And once Hardik comes back, obviously it's going to be good."The coach even suggested India could eventually accommodate both Pandya and Reddy in the same playing XI."Sometimes we could even go on to play both of them in the playing 11," Gambhir said, while stressing that Pandya's current bowling workload remains a factor."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs," he added.Reddy's bowling development excites GambhirGambhir was encouraged by Reddy's progress as a seam-bowling all-rounder and believes having multiple players who can contribute with both bat and ball will give India greater flexibility."I think it's good that we got Nitish now from the Asian Games so that now he can, and you could see the more he bowls, the better he becomes, and we have when you can develop a couple of seam-bowling all-rounders, it will always be handy," Gambhir said.Reddy will now get an opportunity to feature in the ODI series against the West Indies rather than the Asian Games, providing him with additional match exposure.Abhishek's hundred powers India to 3-0 sweepThe Hardik discussion came after India completed a commanding 3-0 T20I series sweep over Afghanistan. Abhishek Sharma smashed a record-breaking 108 off just 34 balls as India posted 221/7 in the third match in New Delhi.Ravi Bishnoi and Reddy then claimed three wickets each as Afghanistan were bowled out for 94, their lowest total against India in T20Is and their heaviest defeat in the format.Gambhir, however, said the focus inside the dressing room remained on impact rather than individual milestones."I can sit here and keep talking about his 100, but it's just the impact. The only thing we talk about in that dressing room is how much impact we create with the bat and how much impact we can create with the ball," Gambhir said.India's 100 runs in the powerplay was another major positive for Gambhir."T20 cricket is not about runs or wickets; it's about how much impact you can create," he said. "The biggest positive was we got a 100 in the powerplay that we have never done in my coaching tenure."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mohammad Rizwan approaches ICC Anti-Corruption Unit over mobile phone seizure by Pakistan's cyber crime agency
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corrupti.
articles.body: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU) for clarity over the seizure of his mobile phone by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). The move comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed his petition challenging the agency’s notices, leaving the Pakistan cricketer seeking answers over the handling of his device and the procedures followed during the ongoing inquiry.According to sources quoted by Geo News, Rizwan submitted an online request through the ICC ACU portal, asking whether the ICC or the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) was aware of, or involved in, the action taken against him.Rizwan seeks clarity over ICC anti-corruption proceduresSources said Rizwan’s request was not intended as a complaint against any individual or organisation. Instead, the Pakistan batter has sought clarification on the procedures followed in his case and the role, if any, of the ICC or ECB in the seizure of his mobile phone.The former Pakistan white-ball captain has also asked whether the process of requesting his phone, transferring it from England to Pakistan and conducting a forensic examination was in accordance with the ICC Anti-Corruption Code.Rizwan has further sought guidance on his responsibilities and the steps he should follow while cooperating with anti-corruption authorities in the future.Lahore High Court dismisses Rizwan’s petitionThe development comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed Rizwan’s petition challenging notices issued to him by the NCCIA. During Thursday’s hearing, Rizwan’s lawyer, Qazi Umair Ali, told Chief Justice Aalia Neelum that the cricketer had been called to a hotel lobby after the Lord’s Test in England and questioned without being served a notice.According to his counsel, Rizwan’s mobile phone was taken into custody after he was assured that it would be returned within three hours. However, the device has not yet been returned.Rizwan’s lawyer also questioned the NCCIA’s jurisdiction, arguing that the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit was the appropriate forum for matters involving alleged corruption-related violations by cricketers. The court directed Rizwan to respond to the NCCIA’s notice before dismissing his petition.NCCIA probe linked to betting and alleged dressing-room leaksThe NCCIA notice relates to an inquiry into online betting and gambling in Pakistan cricket. Reports have also linked the investigation to alleged leaks of information from the Pakistan dressing room during the Test series against England.Rizwan and fellow batter Imam-ul-Haq appeared before the agency in Lahore earlier this month as part of the investigation.No final findings against Rizwan or Imam have been officially announced.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shree Charani’s four-for, Shafali's quick 40 help India beat Japan in Asian Games quater-finals
articles.summary: Cricket News: India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their pl.
articles.body: India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their place in the semi-finals against Bangladesh.The result also sets up a repeat of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 semi-final line-up, with Sri Lanka set to face Pakistan in the other last-four clash.Shree Charani stars as Japan are bowled out for 57After winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers dismantled Japan’s batting line-up, restricting the hosts to just 57 in 19.5 overs. Shree Charani led the charge with a remarkable spell of 4/10, including two maiden overs, to register the best bowling figures by an Indian at the Asian Games. Shafali Verma also chipped in with two wickets for 13 runs.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 balls, but the hosts struggled to build partnerships against India’s disciplined attack.Shafali and Richa wrap up chase in five oversIndia’s chase was emphatic, as they reached the target in just five overs, finishing at 59/2 and winning with 90 balls to spare. Shafali Verma set the tone with a blistering 40 off 15 balls, striking six fours and two sixes. She hammered four boundaries in the opening over and later sealed the victory with a six off Shimako Kato.India had promoted Kamalini and Fulmali up the order, but the move did not pay off, with Kamalini dismissed for a duck and Fulmali scoring six. Shafali then combined with Richa Ghosh, who came in at No. 4, to complete the chase in a hurry.The pair shared a warm hug after the winning hit before crossing over to greet the Japanese players. Japan’s two wickets offered a small positive from an otherwise difficult outing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The defending champions finished the quarter-final with 90 balls to spare, surpassing their previous mark of 84 balls against Thailand in 2022.The record-breaking win at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Friday also sent India into the semi-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, where they will face Bangladesh on Sunday for a place in the medal match.India’s biggest T20I wins by balls remainingBalls remainingOpponentVenueYear90JapanNisshin202684ThailandSylhet202270BangladeshHangzhou202369Sri LankaSylhet202268PakistanDubai2026Shree Charani leads India’s bowling demolitionAfter winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers bundled Japan out for 57 in 19.5 overs. Shreyanka Patil and Deepti Sharma picked up a wicket each.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 deliveries, but the rest of the batting line-up struggled to cope with India’s disciplined bowling. articles.title: Parthiv Patel frontrunner for chief selector if Ajit Agarkar, BCCI fail to agree extension
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong candidate to replace Ajit Agarkar as the men's senior selection committee chai.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong candidate to replace Ajit Agarkar as the men's senior selection committee chairman if the incumbent and the BCCI don't reach an extension agreement.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that Parthiv's name has been circulating in Indian cricket's power corridors for the last six months when key figures were preparing for life after Agarkar. While an extension for the Mumbaikar wasn't off the table back then, a strong cosensus had been reached on Parthiv as the possible successor for the top job.If everything falls into place, Parthiv will be the most senior member of the panel with 25 Tests. SS Das played 23 Tests, RP Singh made 14 appearances while Pragyan Ojha and Ajay Ratra had 24 and 6 caps, respectively. The Indian cricket board has remained tight-lipped on the matter but clarity could be expected in the coming weeks.Agarkar picked the squads for the ODIs and T20Is against West Indies, and the Rest of India team for the Irani Cup and strong murmurs suggest this could well have been his last selection meeting. The former India cricketer attended the India-Afghanistan T20Is in Delhi, accompanied by selectors RP and Ratra. The second game of the series was also attended by ICC Chairman Jay Shah, BCCI President Mithun Manhas and Vice-President Rajeev Shukla.After the Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai on Friday, Shukla was brief on the topic, "AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors."Agarkar recently missed the high-profile review meeting attended by the Indian cricket board's top brass, head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, CoE head VVS Laxman. While the BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia downplayed the chief selector's absence saying he was out of town, those tracking developments believe it "doesn't add up"."You had everyone available there. It's not every day you get the key figures of Indian cricket under the same roof. Head coach travelled from Delhi, Laxman travelled, and Gill and Iyer both juggled their commitments. Mithun Manhas travelled too. So it was a bit strange that the chairman of the men's senior selection committee wasn't there when key issues were on the table. It just doesn't add up," said a source close to developments.Indian cricket is staring at a crucial 12 months in the build-up to the 2027 edition of the ODI World Cup and the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. While a section believes continuity with Agarkar is need of the hour, there are some influential voices keen to hand the reigns to Parthiv.The former India keeper is currently serving as assistant and batting coach at Gujarat Titans and commentating when his schedule permits. It is understood that Parthiv was likely to get a bigger role in the IPL franchise from the next cycle but if the selector role materialises, GT will probably have to explore different options.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI to take call on Ajit Agarkar's future after AGM authorisation, confirms Rajeev Shukla
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection comm.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection committee headed by Ajit Agarkar, vice-president Rajeev Shukla confirmed after the Board's 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai on Friday."Arun Singh Dhumal, Majumdar retain IPL governing council posts; AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors," Shukla said after attending the meeting at the BCCI headquarters.BCCI president Mithun Manhas, vice-president Rajeev Shukla, secretary Devajit Saikia, Bengal Cricket Association president Sourav Ganguly, and Jharkhand State Cricket Association secretary Saurabh Tiwary were among the officials present at the AGM.Agarkar was appointed chairman of the men's senior selection committee in July 2023, and his contract is scheduled to end next month.If his tenure ends without an extension, the BCCI will not be able to appoint a new chairman immediately. The Board will first have to advertise the position and then conduct interviews before naming a replacement, making the appointment process likely to take some time.As reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, former India wicketkeeper-batter Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong contender to replace Agarkar if the BCCI and the current chairman do not agree on an extension.If appointed, Parthiv would become the most experienced member of the current selection panel with 25 Test appearances. The other members are SS Das (23 Tests), RP Singh (14 Tests), Pragyan Ojha (24 Tests) and Ajay Ratra (6 Tests).The selectors announced India's squads for the upcoming home white-ball series against West Indies earlier this week. Their next major responsibility will be selecting India's Test and India 'A' squads for the tour of New Zealand in October and November.India will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests against New Zealand, while India 'A' will play three unofficial Tests against New Zealand 'A' in a shadow tour ahead of the two-match Test series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brewdog's unpaid workers to receive nothing after takeover deal
articles.summary: Administrators say about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and holiday pay and £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.
articles.body:
Former Brewdog staff and several creditors of the collapsed Scottish beer giant are not expected to receive anything from the administration process.

A report from administrators AlixPartners said there were "insufficient funds" for payouts to those owed money by Brewdog's retail arm.

The Aberdeenshire-based brewer had more than £500m of debts when it was sold in March to US drinks firm Tilray in a £33m rescue deal.

Administrators said about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and accrued holiday pay. A further £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.

From a £1bn dream to a brutal collapse: How Brewdog hit the rocks

BrewDog's takeover saw 38 bars close across the UK and £20m in unpaid bills left to hundreds of UK businesses .

Unpaid businesses ranged from coffee shops, bakeries and laundry services, to lawyers, councils and holiday parks.

Creditors included West Ham United FC, Lord's Cricket Ground and Manchester University.

AlixPartners said there were now "insufficient funds" for preferential creditors to be repaid.

This is due to lower than expected funds raised through sales of Brewdog assets and increased costs during the administration period.

The administrators cited unforeseen costs around the security of closed Brewdog pubs after a number of "unauthorised occupiers" gained access.

AlixPartners said it worked with landlords and lawyers to remove them.

The report highlights small amounts of money raised through asset sales. These include:

A 7.8 acre field in Potterton, Aberdeenshire, which sold to a local farmer for £41,300

Nine Brewdog vehicles of "old age and varying roadworthiness" that made only £6,250 from just one sale. The rest were abandoned.

A settlement involving drinks equipment sold to Marylebone Cricket Club, which owns Lords, which generated £62,000.

Parent company BrewDog PLC is still expected to pay its preferential creditor, HMRC, in full for £3.66m tax owed - mainly VAT and excise duty.

Brewdog's biggest debt was to financial services group HSBC, which was owed more than £61m across various banking arms.

It has recovered tens of millions of pounds, but still faces an estimated shortfall of £16.8m.

The report noted that this could be reduced through asset sales in the United States.

Private equity backer TSG, which took a 22% stake in the brewer in 2017, is set to lose £27.6m.

Brewdog also owes around £190m to unsecured creditors. They are expected to receive less than a penny in the pound of what they are owed.

In March 440 staff were made redundant and 736 employees transferred to Tilray, after the US firm bought Brewdog's brand and UK operation.

Eleven bars were retained as part of the sale while 38 other pubs closed immediately.

Former staff can claim for unpaid wages through the UK government's Insolvency Service.

AlixPartners said workers had been given information on this support.

Brewdog's collapse also rendered the shares of about 200,000 crowdfunding investors worthless.

Earlier this year, Alixpartners confirmed that investors in the Equity for Punks scheme would get no return on their shares.

Investors typically spent about £500 on shares - although others invested much larger sums - in return for a stake in the company, discounts and perks.

The administrators stated these shares now had "no value".

Brewdog, which was founded in 2007 by friends James Watt and Martin Dickie, had four breweries and about 100 pubs across the world at its peak.

Watt said he was "heartbroken" after the collapse and apologised to staff and investors.

Brewdog's owner Tilray has been approached for comment.

articles.title: 'Subah Jalandhar, shaam nu Dilli': Abhishek Sharma's fiery Punjabi pep talk before 30-ball century goes viral - Watch
articles.summary: Cricket News: Abhishek Sharma lit up a dead rubber with a 30-ball century as India completed a 3-0 series sweep over Afghanistan with a 127-run win in the third and.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma lit up a dead rubber with a 30-ball century as India completed a 3-0 series sweep over Afghanistan with a 127-run win in the third and final T20I in Delhi on Thursday.Abhishek tore into the Afghanistan bowling attack, scoring 108 off just 34 balls with 11 sixes. His innings took India to 221 for 7 after Afghanistan chose to field first.Afghanistan's batting struggled once again, just as it had in the first two matches, and the visitors were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs.After the match, BCCI posted a video of Abhishek giving a passionate pre-match speech during the team huddle.In the video shared by the BCCI, Abhishek can be seen addressing his teammates during the pre-match huddle in Punjabi and urged them to finish the series strongly."I'm going to speak Punjabi," Sharma declared to his assembled teammates. "So boys, today we are going to play like soormas. Soorma means warriors. The way we've been playing this entire series, that's exactly how we need to finish it today.""Warriors never show mercy to anyone. We aren't letting them off the hook today. It's the last match of the series, look at the crowd, we are going to give them full entertainment. Alright? Otherwise, let's smash it. Chak de phatte, nap de killi, subah Jalandhar, shaam nu Dilli," he added.Abhishek's hundred was the fastest by an Indian in T20Is, breaking Rohit Sharma's 35-ball record set in 2017.It was also the fastest T20I century by a player from a Test-playing nation against another Test-playing nation, going past New Zealand's Finn Allen, who had reached the milestone in 33 balls against South Africa earlier this year.With India having already wrapped up the series, Abhishek's innings added excitement to the final game and capped off a dominant performance before the team heads to the Asian Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship: Somerset title hopes dented with defeat at Yorkshire
articles.summary: Somerset's hopes of a first-ever County Championship title are dented with a heavy defeat at Yorkshire.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Headingley (day four)

Yorkshire 212 & 275: Hill 89, Bess 77; Overton 3-44

Somerset 201: Cliff 8-76 & 101: Lammonby 32; Coad 4-33

Yorkshire (19 pts) beat Somerset (3 pts) by 185 runs

A relentless Yorkshire bowling performance put a significant dent in Somerset's County Championship title challenge, the hosts consigning the pre-game Division One leaders to a hammer-blow defeat at Headingley.

Somerset, who were chasing 287, started day four on 73-3, quickly slipped to 79-6 and were later bowled out for 101 just before 12:00 BST to lose by 185 runs.

A third defeat of the season, and a second against Yorkshire, means that Warwickshire now lead Division One by 11 points from second-placed Somerset, who have never won this title. Nottinghamshire will also be in the mix come next week's final round, even if they lose against Sussex later on Friday.

For the mid-table White Rose, they claimed their fifth win in 13 games and backed up May's success at Taunton. New ball seamers Ben Coad and Ben Cliff starred on Friday, Coad finishing with four wickets and Cliff three.

Outstanding Cliff ended with career-best match figures of 11-105, the 13th best match analysis in his county's first-class history.

Cliff and Coad struck in the space of five balls inside the day's opening half hour, putting Yorkshire on course for a 19-point haul to Somerset's three.

They removed not out batters Tom Lammonby and Tom Abell as Somerset lost two wickets for the addition of only three runs - 76-5.

Lammonby was squared up and caught behind off Cliff for 32 before Abell looped a catch up to backward point off the shoulder of the bat against Coad.

And when Coad struck again almost three overs later, at the end of the 39th, Somerset were in significant trouble, with James Rew caught at second slip on the drive.

Yorkshire came into day four knowing they had the edge but one wicket they were desperate for was that of Craig Overton, who had broken their hearts back in July here with a stunning 79 not out off 30 balls in the Vitality Blast quarter-final.

Cliff got him caught behind pushing forwards in the 42nd over for five, also trapping Lewis Gregory lbw three balls later.

At 88-8, it was all but game over under an overcast Headingley sky but not quite matching the gloomy Somerset outlook.

The Overton and Gregory wickets were Cliff's 10th and 11th in the match following his eight in the first innings.

Like Overton, Migael Pretorius had scored a first-innings fifty. But George Hill had him caught behind, leaving Somerset at 92-9.

Matthew Revis then wrapped things up by yorking Jake Ball, with day four lasting only 82 minutes in all.

Somerset face Surrey at the Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton, in the final round of fixtures, which starts on Thursday, while Yorkshire can continue to play the role of spoilers when they travel to face Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge.

articles.title: 100 years of BCCI! Indian cricket board to form committee for grand year-long celebrations
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) will complete 100 years in 2028 and plans to form a committee to organise year-long celebrations. The.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) will complete 100 years in 2028 and plans to form a committee to organise year-long celebrations. The topic was brought up for discussion during the final phase of the Annual General Meeting (AGM) by an influential administrator and the office bearers unanimously agreed on grand celebrations, commencing in December 2027."The General Body has initiated the process for the BCCI centenary celebrations in 2028. The centenary will be celebrated through a year-long programme, commencing in December 2027 continuing through 2028, marking a landmark milestone in the history of Indian Cricket." read the media advisory.The administrator argued that the BCCI should think globally about the celebrations because of the role it has played in the growth of cricket in different regions."We are talking about the BCCI. 100 years is no ordinary feat. It deserves the grandest celebration which needs careful consideration. Not a one-off affair. articles.title: After getting just one international in 2026-27 season, MCA asks BCCI to allot more matches to Wankhede Stadium
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: The Mumbai Cricket Association has requested the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to allot more international matches to the Wankh.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Mumbai Cricket Association has requested the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to allot more international matches to the Wankhede Stadium in future schedules, while also seeking to be informed before matches are awarded to other venues in Mumbai.The request was made during the 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the BCCI at its headquarters on the Wankhede Stadium premises. MCA secretary Unmesh Khanvilkar submitted a letter, a copy of which is with TOI, putting forward the association's demands.The MCA's request comes after Wankhede was allotted only one international match in India's 2026-27 home season. The stadium will host the third and final ODI between India and Zimbabwe on January 9 next year.The MCA, which celebrated the Wankhede Stadium's 50th anniversary in January 2025, has pointed out that the venue is a permanent Test Centre and has asked the BCCI to consider giving it more international matches.“The MCA sincerely thanks the BCCI for the international matches allotted to Mumbai over the years and for its continued confidence in the Association's hosting capabilities. As the Wankhede Stadium is a permanent Test Centre with a proud history of successfully staging marquee international fixtures, MCA would be grateful if the BCCI could consider allotting a greater number of international matches to the venue in future programmes. We remain committed to providing the highest standards of facilities and match operations for players, officials, and spectators alike,” Khanvilkar has written.The MCA has also asked the BCCI to inform the association before awarding matches to stadiums and venues located within its jurisdiction, which includes Mumbai.The request comes after the BCCI announced a couple of days ago that the 2027 Women's Premier League will be held at the Brabourne Stadium, which is operated by the Cricket Club of India, from January 14 to February 27. Brabourne Stadium is located around 750 metres from Wankhede.The International Cricket Council has also recently awarded the inaugural Women's T20 Champions Trophy matches to Brabourne Stadium. The tournament is scheduled to be held from February 14 to 28.The MCA said being informed in advance would help it deal with queries from its members and other stakeholders and coordinate with the organisations involved in staging matches in Mumbai.“The MCA would be grateful if, as a matter of courtesy, the Association could be kept informed whenever matches are scheduled at stadiums or venues located within its jurisdiction. Such communication would assist MCA in addressing queries from its members and stakeholders and would help foster smooth coordination and cooperation among all concerned,” the MCA has stated in its letter.MCA seeks Under-17 girls' tournamentThe MCA has also asked the BCCI to introduce an Under-17 girls' tournament in its domestic cricket calendar.The BCCI currently conducts a Girls Under-15 tournament, with the next age-group competitions starting at the Under-19 level.“The MCA requests the BCCI to consider introducing a structured Under-17 Girls Cricket Tournament at the national level. Such a tournament would provide an important competitive platform for young female cricketers, strengthen the talent development pathway, and further support the growth of women's cricket across the country,” Khanvilkar has stated in his letter.“We request the Board to give due consideration to the above matters and look forward to a positive response,” Khanvilkar concluded in his letter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship: Hampshire relegated after defeat by Leicestershire
articles.summary: Hampshire are relegated from Division One as Leicestershire chase a target of 334 to keep their own survival hopes alive.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Uptonsteel Grace Road, Leicester (day four)

Hampshire 214 & 363: Gubbins 133; A Patel 4-103

Leicestershire 244 & 335-5: Kelly 86, Cox 75*

Leicestershire (19 pts) beat Hampshire (3 pts) by five wickets

Hampshire have been relegated to Division Two of the County Championship for the first time since winning promotion in 2014 after Leicestershire completed a five-wicket win at Uptonsteel Grace Road.

New Zealand international Nick Kelly and wicketkeeper Ben Cox did the heavy lifting for Leicestershire, backing up skipper Ian Holland's nine-wicket contribution to the win by sharing a 158-run fifth-wicket partnership as the home side chased down the 334 they needed to win.

It wrapped up victory by 14:05 BST with only two wickets lost on the final day.

The result means Leicestershire retain a mathematical chance of survival going into the final week of the season despite the 27-point penalty they were handed on Wednesday for preparing a sub-standard pitch for last month's win over Glamorgan, although it is a near certainty that they too will be playing in Division Two next year.

While the punishment remains subject to appeal, the only way Leicestershire can avoid going down is by wrecking Warwickshire's anticipated title celebrations with victory at Edgbaston next week and in doing so taking 20 more points than Essex pick up from their concluding fixture, away to Glamorgan.

The Foxes, who ended a 23-year-exile from Division One when they were promoted as Division Two champions last season, began the final day needing 178 more runs for victory, with Hampshire looking to take seven more wickets to keep their season alive.

With home supporters eager for the boost of a victory ahead of Sunday's One-Day Cup final against Middlesex, Kelly began with two eye-catching cover drives off Scott Currie for a couple of early boundaries.

Leicestershire suffered a setback as Hamza Shaikh, defending, was caught behind off a thin outside edge, giving Kyle Abbott his 62nd wicket of the campaign.

Yet it became clear the pitch - prepared in much the same away as the offending Glamorgan strip with grass in the middle and two shaved ends - had become somewhat less hazardous for the batting side than earlier in the contest.

Moreover, Hampshire struggled to contain them in any meaningful way. Off-spinner Felix Organ offered control at one end, Abbott was as disciplined as ever and James Fuller tidy, but Manny Lumsden, the 17-year-old who bowled so impressively against Nottinghamshire last week, rarely hit the right lengths this time and leaked runs as a consequence.

The fifth-wicket pair found enough singles too to keep the scoreboard moving without risking too much.

After Cox, who looks unlikely to be with the county next season, had driven Lumsden to the off-side rope to bring the requirement down to exactly 100, Kelly completed his third half-century in Leicestershire colours. Three boundaries then conceded by Lumsden in the final over of the morning left the home side just 67 runs from victory.

Soon afterwards Cox, who has been almost flawless behind the stumps all season, also passed 50 from 76 balls and even the return of Abbott and Currie with the new ball did not change the direction of travel, although there was a reminder the surface still had the capacity to surprise when the left-hander Kelly took a nasty blow on his right-hand.

A couple of painkillers later, though, he was back in full flow, hammering four boundaries in the same over off the unfortunate Lumsden.

Although he was ultimately caught on the rope aiming to finish things in style, the job was all but done, with Cox hitting what turned out to be the winning boundary off a Lumsden no-ball, his eighth of the match.

articles.title: Sehwag shines on debut, Dravid goes ballistic as India U-19 beat Australia by seven runs in Rajkot Youth ODI

articles.body: India Under-19 held off Australia Under-19 by seven runs in a rain-shortened first Youth ODI in Rajkot on Friday, with Anvay Dravid providing the late push and Yashbardhan Chauhan scoring a half-century.The match was reduced to 20 overs per side after rain interrupted play at the Niranjan Shah Stadium. India posted 182 for six after being sent in to bat by Aussie skipper Jack Czosnek, with Chauhan making 54 off 34 balls and Anvay, son of former India captain Rahul Dravid, scoring 38 off 18.The match also marked the India U-19 debut of Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former India cricketer Virender Sehwag. Opening the innings, Aaryavir scored 28 off 26 balls, hitting five fours. His father was present at the venue to watch him play.Australia made a strong start in their chase through openers Neel Patel and Hayden Barbulovic. Patel scored 45 off 31 balls, while Barbulovic made 40 off 24. Australia then remained in the chase through captain Jack Czosnek, who scored 55 off 27 balls.But Czosnek's dismissal in the 19th over ended Australia's hopes. The pair added 69 runs to revive the innings and set up the late charge.Chauhan scored 54, hitting five fours and two sixes. Anvay came in at No. 6 and scored his 38 from just 18 balls, hitting two fours and three sixes. His strike rate of 211.11 gave India the late runs they needed.India scored 108 runs in their final 10 overs.Earlier, Aaryavir made a steady start on his India U-19 debut, opening alongside captain Lakshya Raichandani. articles.title: County Championship: Somerset's title hopes hit badly in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also miss out to leave Warwickshire in command
articles.summary: Somerset lose leadership of Division One to Warwickshire heading into the final round of matches after hugely-costly 185-run defeat to Yorkshire at Headingley; Somerset at home to Surrey, while Warwickshire host Leicestershire in final title-deciding matches from September 24
articles.body:
Top of the County Championship Division One table heading into the penultimate round of matches, Somerset saw rivals Warwickshire wrap up a two-day victory against Essex but failed to keep pace at Headingley.

Chasing 287 - the highest score of the match - they were bundled out for 101 on the final day. Resuming on 73-3 they collapsed horribly as their final seven wickets fell for 25 runs in less than 13 overs.

Ben Cliff took three of them as he finished with 3-29 after taking 8-76 in the first innings, while Ben Coad claimed 4-33 and Matthew Revis 2-7.

The 185-run defeat leaves Somerset chasing from behind heading into their season-ending fixture against Surrey and one step further away from ending their 135-year quest for the county game's top prize.

Warwickshire will take an 11-point lead into the final round with Nottinghamshire also suffering a heavy defeat, while Hampshire have been relegated.

Notts could only set Sussex 76 to win at Hove and, although they grabbed a couple of early wickets to reduce the hosts to 14-2, Sussex secured a seven-wicket win just after the lunch break.

Warwickshire top the table on 203 points and need only to beat Leicestershire in their final game of the season at Edgbaston to be crowned champions for the first time since 2021.

Hampshire's five-wicket defeat by Leicestershire means they are relegated to Division Two.

Leicestershire, deducted 27 points for a breach of ECB pitch regulations earlier this week, will join them if they fail to beat Warwickshire and even a win might not be enough if Essex secure six points against Glamorgan.

articles.title: 'Fifteen days is a long time': BCCI plays wait-and-watch on Ajit Agarkar's future
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia on Friday offered no clear answers on the future of men's selection committe.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia on Friday offered no clear answers on the future of men's selection committee chief Ajit Agarkar but said that "15 days is a long time in the world of cricket.""We still have fifteen days to go. Fifteen days is a long time in the world of cricket. We will take a decision in appropriate time and we will let you know about it. Today, there was no discussion on any individual,” Saikia said after the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting at the BCCI headquarters.This comes after BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla said earlier in the day that the board has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection committee headed by Ajit Agarkar."Arun Singh Dhumal, Majumdar retain IPL governing council posts; AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors," Shukla said after attending the meeting at the BCCI headquarters.BCCI president Mithun Manhas, vice-president Rajeev Shukla, secretary Devajit Saikia, Bengal Cricket Association president Sourav Ganguly, and Jharkhand State Cricket Association secretary Saurabh Tiwary were among the officials present at the AGM.Agarkar was appointed chairman of the men's senior selection committee in July 2023, and his contract is scheduled to end next month.Meanwhile, Saikia also said the BCCI has begun appointing a new five-member junior selection committee. "We have received a very large number of applicants, so we are shortlisting it, and once the shortlisting is completed, then we will give it to our cricket committee, who will be the competent authority to select the selectors for the junior selection committee, so that process is going on, and we are trying to complete it within the next 10-15 days time, to constitute the junior selection committee, because all five selectors' tenure is going to be over very soon," Saikia said.'Lot of time & processes for BCCI to come under Sports Act'Saikia clarified that there was plenty of time before the BCCI would come under the National Sports Governance (NSG) Act. The Supreme Court recently asked the BCCI and its state associations to clarify their position following multiple litigations involving various associations either for minor changes in their constitution or disputes arising from factionalism.Saikia clarified that the BCCI was not averse to coming under the new Sports Act, provided the government completes a few processes."So, regarding the Sports Act, our stand is very clear. There are a lot of things which are yet to be done by the concerned authority; once those exercises are completed, and once BCCI comes under the Sports Act, a particular notification has to be issued to make it a designated sport. Till that time, we are not supposed to do anything. Whenever that notification comes, we will immediately spring into action. We will then do our work as per the new sports rules," Saikia said."We are paying Rs 3,000 crore tax annually to the government. Unlike other sports federations, we don't take any government funding. Hence, cricket cannot be treated as a 'designated sport' under the National Sports Governance Act 2025," Saikia pointed out.Promotion & relegation introduced for domestic umpiresSaikia said that the BCCI will introduce a system of promotion and relegation for umpires in domestic cricket, with 10 umpires being promoted and 10 relegated after every season."All the umpires’ postings will be as per merit. We have an assessing team under the umpires’ board. They will be given assignments according to their merit - whether it is knockouts or important games. After every season, there will be a system of relegation and upgradation. Ten umpires at the end of every season will be promoted, and ten will be relegated. This will make them very alert throughout the season, and that will ultimately help the game of cricket because some players’ futures depend on decisions of the umpires. They have to be very competent and alert," he stated.As reported by TOI on Friday, Saikia confirmed that the BCCI had decided to increase the pay of domestic match referees and umpires from the upcoming season. "There was no revision of fees of the umpires for almost ten years from 2017-18. Earlier there were four categories - A+, A, B, C; now we have restricted it to A, B, C, D. Their per-day fees have been enhanced substantially. We have also enhanced the fee structure of the match referees," Saikia said.'IPL to start from last week of March'Saikia revealed that "IPL-2027 will start from the last week of March." He said that the BCCI has grand plans to celebrate its 100th anniversary (in 2028) and the IPL's 20th anniversary next year. "In Dec 2028, we will complete 100 years of the BCCI, so we will do centenary celebrations from Dec 2027 for one year. The IPL, which will start from March next year, will have its 20th edition. We have discussed that it should be done in a grand way. We have also seen a presentation (on it) after the AGM," Saikia said.Saikia also informed that Shubhadeep Ghosh, who is India's fielding coach, has been appointed on a short-term basis.BGT Test on in RanchiMeanwhile, former India batter Saurabh Tiwary, currently the secretary of the Jharkhand State Cricket Association (JSCA), rubbished reports of Ranchi being replaced as a venue for next year’s Border-Gavaskar Trophy due to poor weather conditions. The marquee five-Test series will begin on Jan 21 in Nagpur, with Chennai, Guwahati, Ranchi and Ahmedabad hosting the other four Tests."There is no change in the venue. If anybody has to write to the BCCI about it, it should be me and I have not written it," Tiwary told the media.“There are six to seven months left (for the Ranchi Test). We don't have any such request or proposal that there are some issues regarding the Ranchi Test,” Saikia said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: As reports of a crisis over the accommodation arrangements start coming in from the Asian Games in Japan, it has emerged that the Indian cr.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As reports of a crisis over the accommodation arrangements start coming in from the Asian Games in Japan, it has emerged that the Indian cricket board (BCCI) has arranged its own accommodation for the men's cricket team."BCCI has arranged its own arrangement for the men’s team since the contingent is much bigger than the permissible number of members because of the size of the support staff. We don’t want to segregate the men’s team during the tournament," BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI."The women’s team is staying in the facilities provided by the organising committee since the size of the contingent is within the permissible number of 20 members," he added.However, Saikia insisted that the BCCI has faith in the local organisation committee to provide satisfactory on-ground facilities at the match venue despite reports of other Asian cricket boards raising objections about the quality of the ground. "We fully trust the organising committee to give the best facilities. This is a big event and I am sure they will do what is required. I'll be reaching there on Oct 1. Only then I can give you a clear picture of the circumstances," he added.'Asiad gold as important as any other title'There have been contrasting views in Indian cricket circles about the board's decision to send a full-strength T20I team to the Asian Games, which coincides with the start of the preparations for next year's ODI World Cup as India are slated to play an ODI series against West Indies at home. India will have at least seven first-choice ODI players playing at the Asian Games. Interestingly, India won the gold medal at the last Asian Games in 2023 with a second-string team as the premier players were held back to prepare for the 2023 ODI World Cup.Saikia asserted that the board's decision was based on the realisation of the value of an Asian Games gold medal. "We are eyeing a gold medal which is very important. We all know India can field three strong teams at a time. We see Asian Games as a very important assignment which can’t be given secondary treatment. That’s why our full-strength team including Bumrah and regular captain Iyer is going. An Asian Games gold is as important as any other big tournament," Saikia stated."I wasn't the secretary when the last Asian Games happened. So, I can't comment on it," he added.'Match against Japan was ICC chair's idea'The BCCI also announced a T20I match against Japan on September 22 to celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations between India and Japan. Saikia revealed that the idea of the match was initiated by ICC chairman Jay Shah. "It’s the initiative of ICC chairman Jay Shah who wants to take cricket to every nook and corner of the world. He made me sit with my Japanese counterpart during the last ICC meet in Edinburgh in July this year. Japan is a country where cricket is growing gradually. Mr. Shah took this initiative and we agreed to the idea," said Saikia.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brydon Carse: Assault investigation dropped by police
articles.summary: England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no further police action after an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby last month is dropped.
articles.body:
England fast bowler Brydon Carse will face no further action from the police after an investigation into an alleged assault in Derby last month was dropped.

Footage of Carse appeared on social media, showing him in handcuffs and surrounded by police on Sunday, 23 August. The footage was captured in the early hours of that day.

It emerged that the 31-year-old had been arrested and then de-arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly.

Later that week, after Carse had been removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan, Derbyshire Police confirmed it was looking at allegations of assault.

In a statement released on Friday, the police said: "An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

"Officers attended Molly Malones in The Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday, 23 August.

"A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers."

Carse will now be subject to an investigation from the Cricket Regulator. The Regulator has not commented. The England and Wales Cricket Board and Carse have both been approached for comment.

The incident in Derby was the latest in a string of late-night alcohol-related controversies to hit the England men's team in the past year.

After Carse was dropped from the second Test against Pakistan, Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and revealed he had addressed his team to make his feelings clear.

Though Carse has continued to be play for his county Durham, he was also left out of the England squads for the third Test against Pakistan and the white-ball series with Sri Lanka.

After he was omitted from the games against Sri Lanka , the ECB confirmed that Carse is available for selection.

"Whilst Brydon was available for selection, he has not been picked for the Sri Lanka series squad," said an ECB statement. "Given recent events, we feel it is important for him to work through the issues that led to the Derby incident and take time for a proper reset.

"This decision does not prejudge the outcome of any investigation."

Earlier this week, England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum said Carse needs to "get his house in order" before returning to international cricket.

Carse did not play in Durham's game against Worcestershire this week. The county said he was "unwell".

articles.body: Brydon Carse will not face any charges after Derbyshire Police ended their investigation into an alleged assault in Derby city centre last month, bringing an end to the legal proceedings that had followed the England fast bowler.The incident had already affected Carse's international career, with the 31-year-old withdrawn from England's squad for the three-Test series against Pakistan after details of the matter emerged. Carse was initially arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly before being de-arrested, while he was not arrested over the separate assault allegation that police subsequently investigated.The incident nevertheless came at a costly time for Carse's England career. articles.title: Adam Zampa scripts history, becomes only second Australian spinner after Shane Warne to reach 200 ODI wickets
articles.summary: Cricket News: Adam Zampa joined Shane Warne as only the second Australian spinner to claim 200 ODI wickets, while Travis Head marked his return to form with a centu.
articles.body: Adam Zampa joined Shane Warne as only the second Australian spinner to claim 200 ODI wickets, while Travis Head marked his return to form with a century as Australia beat Zimbabwe by 84 runs in the second ODI at Harare to seal the series 2-0.Zampa reached the milestone after taking 2/62 in nine overs, dismissing Innocent Kaia and Craig Ervine as Australia successfully defended a target of 357. The leg-spinner became the seventh Australian bowler to reach 200 ODI wickets, joining an elite group led by Glenn McGrath, who tops the country's list with 380 scalps.Zampa joins Warne in Australia's elite spin clubZampa has now taken 201 wickets in 123 ODIs at an average of 29.48. His tally includes 12 four-wicket hauls and one five-wicket haul. Warne remains Australia's leading ODI spinner with 291 wickets in 193 matches, while McGrath is the country's highest overall wicket-taker in the format.Travis Head returns to form with a centuryComing to the match, Head provided the foundation for Australia's imposing total, smashing 112 off 84 balls, including 15 fours and three sixes. The left-hander also crossed the 9,000-run mark in international cricket during his innings.Head has now scored 9,111 runs in 201 international matches and 243 innings at an average of 40.31 and a strike rate of 87.08. His record includes 20 centuries and 43 half-centuries, with a highest score of 175. He shared a 130-run opening partnership with skipper Mitchell Marsh, who scored 53 off 63 balls, including three fours and three sixes. Head then added 60 runs with Cooper Connolly, who contributed 78 off 69 deliveries.A late flourish from Oliver Peake, who struck an unbeaten 41 off just 18 balls, lifted Australia to 356/6. Brad Evans was Zimbabwe's leading bowler, finishing with figures of 3/56.Zimbabwe fall short despite starts from top orderChasing 357, Zimbabwe's top-six batters got starts but failed to convert them into substantial scores. The hosts slipped to 187/5, leaving them with too much to do. Sikandar Raza top-scored with 45 off 49 balls, while Brendan Taylor made 39 off 40 and Craig Ervine scored 38 off 39. Zimbabwe were eventually bowled out for 272 in 48.3 overs.Josh Hazlewood, Connolly, Matthew Renshaw and Zampa took two wickets each as Australia secured an 84-run victory. The win gave Australia an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series, with one ODI still to play.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Cricket News: Bengal cricketer Abishek Porel has been granted bail by a Chinsurah court after spending more than a month in custody in connection with an alleged ra.
articles.body: Bengal cricketer Abishek Porel has been granted bail by a Chinsurah court after spending more than a month in custody in connection with an alleged rape and criminal intimidation case. The development was reported by ABP Ananda, while multiple reports have also confirmed the bail order.Porel, who plays for Delhi Capitals in the IPL, was arrested on August 11 following a complaint filed by a medical student from Karnataka. She alleged that she had been in a relationship with Porel for around three-and-a-half years and that the two had planned to marry.The complainant also alleged that they had travelled abroad together during their relationship, but claimed that Porel later denied their relationship, prompting her to approach the police.Her complaint was filed at Mogra police station on June 23. She also referred to a dispute between the two around one-and-a-half years earlier that had resulted in police intervention, although no formal complaint was filed at that time, according to her account.Police registered a case under Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Sections 311 and 318 and other provisions of the BNS, as well as Sections 66 and 72 of the Information Technology Act.The matter subsequently reached the Calcutta High Court, which directed the police to arrest Porel. The proceedings also included allegations of criminal intimidation and other offences alongside the rape allegation. The court had further directed authorities to seize Porel's electronic devices in connection with concerns over the possible dissemination of photographs of the complainant.Porel was produced before the Chinsurah court after his arrest and was initially denied bail before being sent to judicial custody. He has now been granted bail after spending 36 days in jail, according to the ABP Ananda report.Porel has previously denied the allegations against him.Porel's IPL and domestic careerThe 23-year-old wicketkeeper-batter has been part of the Delhi Capitals setup since 2023, when he made his IPL debut. He scored 108 runs in four innings for the franchise during the 2026 season. Overall, he has played 35 games, scoring 769 runs at an average of 25.63 and a strike rate of 145.37, including four fifties.Porel made his first-class debut for Bengal in the 2021-22 season and has since become an established figure in the domestic circuit. He has represented Bengal in 32 first-class matches and 23 List A games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Both the trophies will come': BCCI's big update on Asia Cup trophies snubbed by Mohsin Naqvi
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Asia Cup trophies won by India's men's and women's teams remain in Dubai, but BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has assured that both pieces of silver.
articles.body: The Asia Cup trophies won by India's men's and women's teams remain in Dubai, but BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has assured that both pieces of silverware will eventually make their way to the board's headquarters in Mumbai.Saikia confirmed the development after the BCCI's 95th Annual General Meeting in Mumbai on Friday, although he stopped short of specifying when the trophies would arrive. The men's and women's teams had both declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi, leaving the silverware at the ACC headquarters in Dubai."Asia Cup trophies, we hope it will come one day," Saikia said in Mumbai on Friday after the BCCI's 95th Annual General Meeting.“I will not give you a timeline, but I can assure you that both the trophies will come up and land up in this BCCI head office at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai,” he added.The latest development follows India's women's team refusing to attend the trophy presentation after beating Sri Lanka in the Women's T20 Asia Cup final last week. Harmanpreet Kaur's side did not appear at the presentation ceremony with Naqvi on the dais, while a similar situation had unfolded after India's men's team won the Asia Cup last year.The women's team instead conducted its own medal presentation after the final, with BCCI secretary Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla presenting Nandni Sharma with the fielding medal. The official ceremony later saw Naqvi present the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka.Saikia had already made the BCCI's position clear a day after the women's final, describing the decision not to accept the trophy from Naqvi as a "firm institutional decision".“Our position had been communicated to the ACC in advance that the Indian team would not participate in the trophy presentation under the circumstances. Given the circumstances and the sentiments prevailing in the country, the BCCI felt that it would not be appropriate for the team to receive the trophy in the proposed manner,” Saikia told news agency PTI.“This was a firm institutional decision, reflective of the position we have maintained, and was not directed at the players, the tournament or the sport,” he added.The issue could have implications beyond the Asia Cup, with India and Pakistan both competing at the Asian Games in Japan. The Asian Games cricket tournament is being conducted under the ACC, while both Indian teams are among the contenders for gold. The possibility of Naqvi being involved in a medal presentation could therefore become another point of attention.Saikia's latest comments also come with Naqvi's current term as ACC president approaching its scheduled conclusion in April 2027. Whether he receives an extension will depend on the support of ACC members.The strained cricketing relationship between India and Pakistan has remained evident since the Pahalgam terror attack, with players from the two teams having refused to shake hands with each other in subsequent encounters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: At 18, he hit a century on Test debut and was hailed as the next Sachin Tendulkar; 9 years later, Prithvi Shaw is still fighting for a comeback amid an engagement split
articles.summary: Cricket News: Prithvi Shaw once looked destined to become one of Indian cricket’s next big batting stars. A teenage prodigy who led India to the Under-19 World Cup .
articles.body: Prithvi Shaw once looked destined to become one of Indian cricket’s next big batting stars. A teenage prodigy who led India to the Under-19 World Cup title and scored a century on his Test debut, Shaw was compared with Sachin Tendulkar and tipped for a long international career. But years later, the Mumbai batter finds himself outside India’s plans, with his career at a crucial juncture.Shaw’s journey has featured early success, flashes of brilliance, injuries and inconsistent returns. While he continues to pursue opportunities in domestic cricket and the IPL, his recent personal-life headlines, including the end of his engagement to Akriti Agarwal, have added another chapter to a career that has taken an unexpected turn.From Mumbai’s cricketing system to Under-19 World Cup gloryBorn on November 9, 1999, Shaw emerged through Mumbai’s cricketing system and quickly became known for his attacking batting. His performances at junior level brought him into the national spotlight, and he was soon regarded as one of India’s most exciting young prospects.The breakthrough came in 2018, when Shaw captained India to the Under-19 World Cup title in New Zealand. His performances with the bat and leadership of the side strengthened his reputation as a player to watch.Later that year, Shaw made his Test debut against West Indies in Rajkot, and made an immediate impact. He scored a century in his first Test, announcing himself on the international stage and fuelling comparisons with Tendulkar.A dream start to international cricketShaw’s Test debut was followed by a promising start to his international career, but he struggled to secure a regular place across formats. He made his ODI debut against New Zealand in February 2020 and played his first T20I against Sri Lanka in July 2021. His last appearance for India came in 2021, and he has not featured in the national team since.In five Tests, Shaw scored 339 runs at an average of 42.37, including one century and two half-centuries. His highest score was 134. In six ODIs, he made 189 runs, with a best of 49.Domestic cricket: A route back to the national setupWith international selection no longer within immediate reach, domestic cricket has become central to Shaw’s hopes of a comeback. A long-time Mumbai player, Shaw moved to Maharashtra for the 2025-26 domestic season. His first-class record has demonstrated his ability to score heavily, but rebuilding his international prospects requires sustained performances rather than isolated big innings.IPL journey: Flashes of promise, but no sustained breakthroughShaw’s attacking style also made him a prominent name in the Indian Premier League. He spent several seasons with Delhi Capitals, where his aggressive approach at the top of the order offered the franchise quick starts.However, his IPL career has not consistently produced the sustained performances needed to push him back into India’s plans. His time with Delhi ended after the 2024 season, and he returned to the franchise setup in 2026. The IPL remains a major platform for Shaw, but turning his talent into consistent returns will be key if he hopes to revive his international career.The biggest hurdle in Prithvi Shaw’s bid to return to India’s team has been a combination of inconsistent performances, fitness concerns and disciplinary issues not one isolated setback. His difficulties became particularly visible during the 2024 domestic season, when he was reportedly dropped from Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy side over concerns about his fitness and attendance at practice sessions. Shaw later acknowledged that he had reduced his practice hours and lost focus, while his omission from Mumbai’s squad and subsequent move to Maharashtra marked a fresh phase in his career. The switch offered him an opportunity to rebuild, but a comeback still depends on sustained performances and consistency across domestic cricket and the IPL.Engagement with Akriti Agarwal called offAway from cricket, Shaw’s relationship with Akriti Agarwal also attracted attention after the couple announced their engagement in March 2026. Agarwal later confirmed that they had decided to separate, citing different goals and circumstances for the future. She described the decision as mutual and requested privacy, asking people not to speculate about their personal lives.The separation is a development in Shaw’s personal life; there is no linking it to his cricketing career or selection prospects.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli or Rohit Sharma: Pat Cummins names 'toughest' India player he faced
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pat Cummins has faced some of India's biggest cricketing names during his international career, but when asked to identify the toughest Indian opponen.
articles.body: Pat Cummins has faced some of India's biggest cricketing names during his international career, but when asked to identify the toughest Indian opponent he has come up against, the Australia captain did not pick MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli or Rohit Sharma.Instead, Cummins went back to the player who repeatedly tested Australia's patience during two memorable Border-Gavaskar Trophy series and chose Cheteshwar Pujara as his toughest Indian opponent.The Australia Test and ODI captain made the admission in a recent promotional video for Prime Video Sport, where he was asked to name the toughest player he had faced from India, Pakistan, New Zealand, England, Sri Lanka, South Africa and the West Indies.For India, there was little hesitation in his choice.“India, I'm going to say, Pujara. Really hard to get out. Just like death by a thousand papercuts. Happy to face 100 dot balls if he wanted to. Not going to give you a chance,” said Cummins in a video shared on social media.Pujara's reputation as an immovable presence at the crease was particularly evident against Australia. He played 25 Tests against them and accumulated 2,074 runs at an average of 49.38.Nearly half of those runs, 993, came in Australia, where Pujara struck three centuries and five fifties. His highest score Down Under was 193.The 2018-19 and 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy series remain synonymous with Pujara's determined resistance against Australia's pace attack, including Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.Pujara retired from international cricket last year after a career spanning 103 Tests for India. He finished with 7,195 runs at an average of 43.6, including 19 centuries and 35 fifties.Cummins' other picksCummins selected Brendon McCullum as his toughest opponent from New Zealand, recalling the former New Zealand captain's aggressive approach at the top of the order.“From New Zealand, I played Brendon McCullum a couple of times when he was really going hard at the top of the order," said Cummins.For Pakistan, Cummins opted for former spinner Saeed Ajmal, “Pakistan, Saeed Ajmal. It was like the last ball of the over; I walked in, Saeed Ajmal just goes, and I went, what? Clean bowled. I have never seen anything like that," Cummins said.His selections from the remaining countries were equally notable. Sir Alastair Cook was his choice from England, AB de Villiers from South Africa, Tillakaratne Dilshan from Sri Lanka and Chris Gayle from the West Indies.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Main jhooth nahi bolunga’: Rohit Sharma reveals the comfort food he craved during sleepless Test-match nights
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former India captain Rohit Sharma has revealed the unlikely comfort food he would turn to during sleepless nights in the middle of Test mat.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India captain Rohit Sharma has revealed the unlikely comfort food he would turn to during sleepless nights in the middle of Test matches, recalling how the pressure of his favourite format often left him nervous and craving a late-night snack.Rohit, who played 67 Tests for India between 2013 and 2024, opened up about his midnight cravings on his television show, ‘Family Full House with Rohit Sharma’. He revealed that his mother's homemade banana wafers became his go-to comfort food during those long nights on Test match duty.“Haan, hoti toh hai. Main jhooth nahi bolunga, lekin jab bhi main Test match khelta tha, andar bahut nervousness hoti thi. Toh Test match ke time khaas karke, kyunki yeh mera favourite format tha, Test match khelna,” Rohit said.The former opener called time on his Test career last year after scoring 4,301 runs in 67 matches at an average of 40.57, including 12 centuries and 18 fifties. His highest score in the format was 212.‘Nervousness mein mujhe neend nahi aati thi’Rohit explained that the demands of Test cricket often made it difficult for him to switch off after a day's play.“Kyunki Test match khelna aasaan format nahi hai. Koi bhi format aasaan nahi hota, lekin Test match ke apne alag-alag challenges hote the. Toh Test match ke liye main hamesha nervous rehta tha aur nervousness mein mujhe neend nahi aati thi, toh raat bhar main jaaga rehta tha,” he said.Those sleepless nights, in turn, often brought with them the urge to eat something.“Toh aap jaage rehte ho toh kuch na kuch khaane ka mann karta tha. Toh main hamesha mere saath mera comfort food rakhta tha, jo meri mummy hamesha bana ke deti thi, woh tha banana wafers,” Rohit said.The snack came with a personal touch. Rohit revealed that the banana wafers were made by his mother, who used a baking method rather than frying them.His mother's homemade midnight snack“Woh fried nahi hota tha. Meri mummy ke kuch tareeke the, woh bake karti thi usko aur woh main hamesha apne saath leke chalta tha. Toh kabhi bhi mann karta tha toh usse kha leta tha,” he said.For a batter who spent years dealing with the mental and physical demands of the longest format, the simple homemade snack offered a familiar taste of home during the intensity of Test cricket.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Selection committee has made up its mind': Ex-India cricketer on Rishabh Pant's exclusion from West Indies ODIs
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra believes the Indian selectors have made up their mind about Rishabh Pant’s immediate future in white-ball cricket.
articles.body: Former India cricketer Aakash Chopra believes the Indian selectors have made up their mind about Rishabh Pant’s immediate future in white-ball cricket.Pant was left out of India’s ODI squad for the upcoming West Indies series. However, he has been named captain of the Rest of India side for the Irani Cup.The three-match ODI series against the West Indies will begin in Thiruvananthapuram on September 27. The second ODI will be played in Guwahati on September 30, while the third match will take place in New Chandigarh on October 3.Chopra said the different roles given to Pant in red-ball and white-ball cricket show how India currently view the wicketkeeper-batter.‘A very strange and very unique case’Chopra said Pant remains an important player in Test cricket, but his place in the ODI team appears to have changed.“Rishabh Pant is a very strange and very unique case. While he is playing Test cricket and is a very important member of the red-ball side, he was stripped of his vice-captaincy duties there as well. But in ODI cricket, without playing, he’s been bid goodbye," Chopra told Jio Star.He also pointed to Pant being named captain of the Rest of India side for the Irani Cup as another sign of his importance in red-ball cricket."At the same time, he has been made the captain of the Rest of India (ROI), which also tells you that, with respect to red-ball cricket, they are very serious about Rishabh playing a huge role in the longer format. But for white-ball cricket, as of now, I think this selection committee has made up its mind,” he added.Pant’s ODI future unclearPant has never been a permanent member of India’s 50-over squad and has played only one ODI in the past four years. He was also dropped from the T20I team after India’s 2024 T20 World Cup victory.His latest ODI omission comes as India start their preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Shubman Gill will captain the team against the West Indies, with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli also part of the 15-member squad.Dhruv Jurel is among the wicketkeeping options, while KL Rahul has been named vice-captain in place of Shreyas Iyer. Iyer will be part of India’s Asian Games campaign.Competition for World Cup spotsChopra also spoke about the competition for places in India’s wider ODI group as the team prepares for the 2027 World Cup.“You have to think about who you can take along as reserves for the World Cup. So, there will be a toss-up here between Yashasvi Jaiswal and Ruturaj Gaikwad, who are both part of this team, and whenever they’ve played, they’ve scored a lot of runs. So, I’m looking at an opportunity opening up for one of these two," Chopra said.He also backed fast bowler Auqib Nabi to make the most of his opportunity if he gets one."Auqib Nabi has been travelling with the team for some time now but isn’t getting a chance to play in the XI.
