articles.title: ‘Only expectation from Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli is to keep scoring runs’: Aakash Chopra ahead of West Indies ODIs
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: With the 2027 ODI World Cup now just over a year away, former India batter Aakash Chopra believes Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli do not need .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With the 2027 ODI World Cup now just over a year away, former India batter Aakash Chopra believes Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli do not need to prove anything beyond what they have already done — they simply need to keep scoring runs.Rohit and Kohli are set to return to India’s ODI side for the three-match home series against the West Indies, beginning in Thiruvananthapuram on September 27. With Shubman Gill leading the side and KL Rahul named vice-captain, the experienced duo’s form will be one of the major talking points as India begin to shape their plans for the World Cup in South Africa.“The World Cup is just one year away now, and I know that if Rohit and Kohli get in, they will score runs, win you matches, and possibly win you trophies. So, looking at it from this perspective, the only expectation from Rohit and Kohli is just this: keep scoring runs,” Chopra told JioHotstar’s ‘Follow the Blues’.‘They’ll score runs, win you matches’Both batters have remained productive in ODIs this year. Kohli has scored 384 runs in six innings at an average of 64.00 and a strike rate of over 106, with a century and three fifties.Rohit, meanwhile, has made 379 runs in nine innings at an average of 42.11 and a strike rate of over 99. His tally includes a century and a fifty, with his best score being 138 against England at Lord’s.For Chopra, their experience could become particularly valuable as India move towards the next World Cup.Rohit and Kohli are part of the 15-member squad for the West Indies ODIs alongside Ruturaj Gaikwad, Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul. Shreyas Iyer, who has been part of India’s recent ODI plans, is unavailable as he leads the Asian Games campaign.Chopra also backed the selectors’ overall composition of the squad, including the decision to bring in Dhruv Jurel as the second wicketkeeper.“With the available players, you try and make the most of what you have. The biggest change you notice is that KL Rahul has been made vice-captain in place of Shreyas Iyer because Shreyas Iyer will be at the Asian Games. There was certainly a question mark over Rishabh Pant, but I also liked Dhruv Jurel’s selection. So, considering all of that, a very good team has been picked, and full marks to the Indian team selectors,” he said.Jaiswal-Gaikwad reserve battle, Pant’s white-ball futureChopra also identified a potential battle between Jaiswal and Gaikwad for a reserve batting spot ahead of the 2027 World Cup.“You have to think about who you can take along as reserves for the World Cup. So, there will be a toss-up here between Yashasvi Jaiswal and Ruturaj Gaikwad, who are both part of this team, and whenever they have played, they have scored a lot of runs. So, I am looking at an opportunity opening up for one of these two. Auqib Nabi (maiden ODI call-up for West Indies series) has been travelling with the team for some time now, but is not getting a chance to play in the XI. If he gets his opportunity, I will be quite excited to see him perform.”Chopra also spoke about Rishabh Pant’s omission from the ODI squad, despite his continued importance in the longer format.“Rishabh Pant is a very strange and very unique case. While he is playing Test cricket and is a very important member of the red-ball side, he was stripped of his vice-captaincy duties there as well. But in ODI cricket, without playing, he has been bid goodbye. At the same time, he has been made the captain of the Rest of India (ROI), which also tells you that, with respect to red-ball cricket, they are very serious about Rishabh playing a huge role in the longer format. But for white-ball cricket, as of now, I think this selection committee has made up its mind,” he said.The series will also provide an opportunity for Ravindra Jadeja and Nitish Kumar Reddy, with Chopra highlighting the competition for all-rounder spots ahead of the World Cup.“One big highlight, in my opinion, was pulling Nitish Kumar Reddy out of the Asian Games and playing him here. So, if Hardik Pandya is not available someday, they really want somebody who can bowl pace and bat as well. Ravindra Jadeja will have to, of course, take wickets and score runs. Fielding has always been his strong suit. But from a World Cup point of view, you have Axar Patel, Ravindra Jadeja, and Washington Sundar, and not all of them will go to South Africa. So, someone will be left out, and therefore, every time you get an opportunity, you have to grab it with both hands,” he said.India face the West Indies in the second ODI in Guwahati on September 30 before the series concludes in Chandigarh on October 3.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Sri Lanka: Harry Brook and Jos Buttler lead hosts to top of rankings
articles.summary: England steamroller Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.
articles.body:
Sri Lanka 124 all out (18.5 overs): Nissanka 36 (24), K Mendis 35 (28); Baker 2-17, Archer 2-23, Jacks 2-31

England 126-2 (9.4 overs): Buttler 62* (32), Brook 33 (21)

England won by eight wickets, won series 3-0

England steamrollered Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.

Watched by new Test coach Stephen Fleming, England once again outclassed the tourists to conclude a one-sided series played on the fringe of autumn.

England's pace bowlers were outstanding in dismissing Sri Lanka for a paltry 124, then the home side chased the target in 9.4 overs.

Jamie Overton conceded only 15 runs in his four overs, including taking a wicket. Sonny Baker's improvement continued with 2-17 and Jofra Archer recovered from an expensive start to return 2-23.

England's fielding was sharp, best demonstrated by Liam Dawson's direct hit to run out Eshan Malinga.

The target was never likely to pose a challenge to an England batting line-up that remains powerful despite Phil Salt and Jacob Bethell being absent injured.

Though opener Aneurin Donald was out for 13, Jos Buttler and Harry Brook strolled the pursuit with a second-wicket stand of 85.

Brook was run out for 33, leaving Buttler to wrap it up with a six that left him unbeaten on 61.

The victory by eight wickets was concluded with 62 balls to spare - the most for England in a home T20 international.

The success was England's 23rd win in 26 completed T20s since Brook took charge in the summer of 2024. They have reclaimed their number one ranking from India.

The pity for this group is a rare lengthy wait until the next global T20 tournament. The next men's T20 World Cup is not until 2028, the same year T20 cricket makes its debut in the Olympics.

England are instead building towards a 50-over World Cup in southern Africa in the autumn of 2027. Three one-day internationals against the Sri Lankans begin in Durham on Tuesday.

Buttler crunches 62 not out as England seal 3-0 series win - as it happened

Seamers another sign of England's versatility

A feature of England's success in this format has been captain Brook's heavy use of spin bowling. On this occasion the spinners took a backseat – Adil Rashid and Dawson sent down only four overs between them.

Instead, it was the seamers to the fore, even without the variations of Sam Curran, another England player absent injured.

Baker endured difficult debuts in all three international formats, yet in this series has started to show his potential.

After Archer's first over went for 15, Baker had Lahiru Udara sky to wicketkeeper Buttler. He later returned to wrap up the innings, taking the final wicket when Dilshan Madushanka skied to Brook.

Archer was a spectator for some time after his initial struggle. When he returned, he got the dangerous Kamindu Mendis to pull to deep mid-wicket for 35.

Archer's second wicket was curious – Wanindu Hasaranga out hit-wicket attempting a slog, his bat almost placed on top of the bails.

Overton was the pick, returning his most economical figures when bowling his full allocation of four in a T20 international.

Though Tom Banton dropped a catch slipping on the greasy outfield, England's fielding was otherwise exceptional.

Brook took a sharp catch at mid-wicket to remove Pathum Nissanka for 36, Rashid was alert enough to run out Charith Asalanka and Dawson's direct hit was the coup de grace.

Donald misses chance before Buttler-Brook show

At the age of 29, Donald has been given an international opportunity in this series as a replacement for Salt.

He has shown only glimpses of his excellent domestic form, returning a high score of 21. On this occasion, he tried to wallop the spin of Tharindu Rathnayake over long-on and was stumped by a distance.

In Buttler and Brook, the captains past and present, England have two men in supreme form. Buttler is England's best white-ball batter of all-time, while Brook is on the way to being one of their greats.

Such is their quality, the second-wicket pair turned the remainder of the chase into little more than a glorified net.

Sri Lanka were scruffy – they conceded 17 runs in wides. The hapless nature of the visitors' display was epitomised when Brook should have been caught off Madushanka, only for keeper Kamil Mishara and point fielder Nissanka to look at each other as the ball dropped to the ground.

There was no need for Brook to attempt a single that Hasaranga fielded in his follow-through, the bowler hitting direct with a throw at the non-striker's end.

Buttler won it in the following over, clubbing 18 from four Malinga deliveries, with two maximums hammered over the leg side.

articles.title: The Blaze beat Hampshire in last-ball thriller to win One-Day Cup
articles.summary: Emma Jones seals the Blaze's treble success with a dramatic last-ball boundary to win a thrilling One-Day Cup final and shatter Hampshire's hopes of silverware.
articles.body:
Women's Metro Bank One-Day Cup final, Trent Bridge

Hampshire 251-9 (50 overs): McCaughan 78, Kemp 52; Higham 4-49, Phillips 3-38

The Blaze 254-7 (50 overs): Beaumont 74, Elwiss 64; Wellington 3-36

Emma Jones sealed The Blaze's treble success with a dramatic last-ball boundary to win a thrilling One-Day Cup final and shatter Hampshire's hopes of silverware.

The Blaze, who had already won the T20 Blast and County Cup trophies this season, seemed to be coasting towards their target of 252 after half-centuries from Tammy Beaumont (74) and Georgia Elwiss (64) at the Utilita Bowl.

But Hampshire's spinners fought back, with Amanda-Jade Wellington taking 3-36 and Bex Tyson 2-46 as four wickets went down for 29 to leave the Blaze needing 30 from the final three overs.

However, Jones kept her cool with an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls and, with two still required from Daisy Gibb's final delivery, pulled it to the boundary to clinch a remarkable treble for her side.

That meant heartbreak for Hampshire on home soil for a second successive year, having lost the 2025 final to Lancashire.

Asked to bat after Blaze captain Kirstie Gordon won the toss, Hampshire started slowly but Ella McCaughan and Maia Bouchier gradually eased into their rhythm to share an opening stand of 84 from 106.

Women's One-Day Cup final: Blaze seal dramatic win over Hampshire with final ball of match

Bouchier, who had hit hundreds in both of her past two innings, took a liking to the bowling of Lucy Higham, driving the off-spinner twice for leg-side boundaries – but then she tried to do it a third time and picked out the long-on fielder.

Hampshire skipper Georgia Adams departed cheaply, smacking Higham's full toss to mid-off, but McCaughan eased past her half-century as Freya Kemp seized control, hitting the spinners cleanly over the top and smashing Higham for the first six of the innings.

However, having reached 166-2, Hampshire began to stutter as Grace Ballinger returned for a second spell to trap McCaughan lbw for 78 and Kemp (52 from 46) was lured down the track by Higham (4-49) and stumped.

Wickets continued to tumble as Charley Phillips (3-38) struck three times in rapid succession and Gordon, whose consistent 10 overs cost just 39, produced an outstanding one-handed catch at mid-on to remove Naomi Dattani.

Gibb and Poppy Tulloch did just enough to haul Hampshire above the 250 mark in the final over of the innings, but their hopes of capturing early wickets in the Blaze response proved forlorn.

Beaumont struck back-to-back fours off Dattani to raise the 50 partnership well before the end of the powerplay and Adams went for 13 in her second over as Sarah Bryce walloped her high over the long-on boundary.

It was Wellington who raised Hampshire spirits by dismissing both Bryce sisters in the same over, with Sarah sweeping to deep square leg before Kathryn was brilliantly taken by Adams at slip, leaping low to her left.

Elwiss provided a calming influence, milking singles and rotating the strike effectively with the former England batter, who passed 50 from 75, albeit riding her luck at times with some aerial shots and risky singles.

The opener was put down by Kemp, diving forward at deep midwicket, while Rhianna Southby missed a stumping chance off Tyson soon afterwards – but Beaumont's good fortune eventually ran out when Wellington landed one bang on her left foot and in front.

Elwiss, who brought up her 50 with successive fours off Wellington, then took up the baton – but The Blaze still needed 51 when she fell to Tyson, whose spell of 2-46 helped to stifle the batters as boundaries dried up almost entirely.

Hampshire looked favourites, only for Jones to take two fours off the penultimate over from Dattani and, despite the run-out of Higham with three required, her composure was enough to guide the Blaze home.

articles.title: England hammer Sri Lanka to return top of T20 world rankings as 3-0 series sweep clinched at Emirates Old Trafford
articles.summary: Jos Buttler smacks unbeaten 62 off 32 balls as England chase 125-run target in only 9.4 overs to make it 15 T20 international wins in a row over Sri Lanka; watch the first ODI between the two teams on Tuesday from 12pm, live on Sky Sports Cricket (first ball 12.30pm)
articles.body:
Off the back of 119-run and six-wicket wins in the opening two games, Harry Brook's side clinched a 3-0 series sweep as his 33 off 21 balls, plus Jos Buttler's unbeaten 62 off 32 fired the hosts to their 125-run target in a mere 9.4 overs.

Aneurin Donald (13 off 6) could only manage a brief cameo with the bat for the third time in the series - stumped off Tharindu Ratnayake - while Brook was run out just shy of victory, one that Buttler clinched with a stunning one-handed six over deep midwicket to make it 15 wins in a row for England against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals.

The visitors had earlier been bowled out for a paltry 124 in 18.5 overs after being inserted by England, with Sonny Baker (2-17), Jofra Archer (2-23) and Will Jacks (2-31) picking up a couple apiece as the wickets were generously shared around.

Pathum Nissanka (36 off 24) had briefly given cause for optimism - despite the early wickets of Lahiru Udara (10), to a strong catch from Buttler in the swirling wind, and Kamil Mishara (2) - as he cleared the rope on three occasions in the opening powerplay.

Nissanka was a touch unlucky to ultimately perish in the seventh over, with Brook taking a terrific, diving catch at midwicket off one nailed out of the middle of the Sri Lankan opener's bat.

Skipper Charith Asalanka's innings was a sedentary 16 off 14 deliveries before being run out by Jacks - only just - after he nearly missed the stumps altogether with his take at the non-striker's end.

Kamindu Mendis (35 off 28) struck a couple of heavy-handed blows, but he too was lacking in support and the Sri Lankan collapse was well and truly in force by the time he picked out Jacks on the deep midwicket fence.

The tourists lost their last six wickets for 17 runs in less than five overs, with Wanindu Hasaranga's dismal departure - hit wicket off Archer after nearly swinging himself off his feet - pretty symptomatic of Sri Lanka's struggles in the series.

And they have got little time to rectify things for the three-match one-day international series which follows and gets under way in Durham on Tuesday.

Brook: No 1 ranking an 'amazing' achievement

England captain and player of the series Harry Brook :

"Being back at world No 1 in T20s is an amazing achievement and one everyone should be really proud of.

"Everyone stepped up, especially lads who haven't played as much.

"For Sonny Baker to bowl three overs in the powerplay in two games is an amazing achievement, not going for many runs and taking wickets.

"We want to be a side when the conditions aren't in our favour where we are still able to manufacture a win.

"That might not be the prettiest but we are doing it extremely well and are trending in the right direction."

"England have been superb. They look a much better team than Sri Lanka but look well-oiled and seem to know what they are doing.

"Even players you might not feel are in the best 11 - remember, England are missing Phil Salt, Sam Curran and Jacob Bethell through injury - appear like they know what they are doing.

"With clear roles and responsibility, you get good performances and that's what nearly every player has produced in this series."

articles.title: Metro Bank One Day Cup women's final: The Blaze beat Hampshire in final-ball thriller to secure domestic treble
articles.summary: Emma Jones hit an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls for The Blaze and scored the winning runs off the final ball of the match in Southampton after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had recorded half-centuries against Hampshire for whom Ella McCaughan top-scored with 78
articles.body:
The Trent Bridge-based side had already lifted the Vitality Blast and Vitality T20 County Cup but were forced to dig deep after needing 17 from the last two overs and then two off the final ball. Emma Jones was the hero with an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls and scored the winning runs - after Tammy Beaumont and Georgia Elwiss had scored half-centuries in the chase of 252.

Earlier, Lucy Higham had taken 4-49 to help restrict Hampshire - who were also losing finalists in 2025 - to 251, with Ella McCaughan and Freya Kemp whacking fifties in vein. The Blaze won the toss and, through the miserliness of Grace Ballinger and Charley Phillips, only allowed 11 runs in the first five overs. But Hampshire's opening pair of the super-in-form Maia Bouchier and McCaughan slowly began to turn the tide in their direction with an 84-run stand. McCaughan confidently pinged the ball around for her first fifty since June.

Bouchier, who was dropped on a duck, could not make it three centuries in a row when she holed out to long-on before Georgia Adams slapped straight to mid-off shortly afterwards - both to Higham. The hosts kicked back as McCaughan and Kemp dominated the middle overs with a 67-run stand and were 166-2 in the 32nd over. But The Blaze used their final nous to pull things back. Higham added wickets three and four of the afternoon by having Kemp stumped and Naomi Dattani caught brilliantly by Kirstie Gordon at mid-on. The spinner has taken 14 wickets in eight matches since her return from The Hundred - with this 4-49, her third four-for in that period. Pacer Phillips dismissed Rhianna Southby, Abi Norgrove and Amanda-Jade Wellington in three overs in a row, as Hampshire slumped and could only reach 251.

In response, Sarah Bryce and Beaumont made mincemeat of the bowlers for 15 overs, as they strode towards the target. The pair put on 95 with relative ease, and then Wellington spun things by seeing off both Bryce sisters in an over - Sarah was caught at deep square before Kathryn was superbly caught at slip. Beaumont, with the help of Elwiss, kept things ticking, although the former England opener lived a charmed life - she was dropped three times and also survived a stumping chance. Her luck ran out, having scored her fifth half-century of the campaign, when she was lbw to Wellington - sparking three wickets to fall in 26 balls. And with 30 still needed, Gordon was caught. It meant there was 17 required from the last two overs, but Jones took the sting out of things. A ridiculous reverse pull and a straight drive both went to the boundary, and despite a run out with the third ball, Jones took her side to victory with a swept four off the final ball of a nerve-filled match.

articles.title: Bill Madden: The 20-something stars are taking over MLB’s award races this season
articles.summary: NEW YORK — In the absence of Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge, the mysterious power outages of Vlad Guerrero Jr. and Cal Raleigh, and the injuries to Tarik Skub...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — In the absence of Shohei Ohtani and Aaron Judge , the mysterious power outages of Vlad Guerrero Jr. and Cal Raleigh , and the injuries to Tarik Skubal and Garrett Crochet , baseball's postseason awards are coming into focus by ushering in a new wave of 20-something superstars.

Going into the weekend the teams with the best records in each league were the small market Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays , both of which with leading candidates for baseball's postseason hardware who are still years away from their prime.

For the Brewers, 24-year-old Jacob Misiorowski is the runaway leader for the NL Cy Young Award, at 15-5 and leading the majors in ERA (1.89), strikeouts (243), WHIP (0.812) and strikeouts per nine innings (13.1) — while the Rays, in their bid to salt away the AL East, have gotten a late boost from their 23-year old third baseman Junior Caminero , who took over the AL home run lead last week and was neck and neck with Houston 's Yordan Alvarez in RBIs and total bases.

On the surface, Alvarez, who leads the AL in OPS and batting (.311), would appear to have the overall statistical edge on Caminero for the MVP. But the fact that Alvarez is a DH and Caminero, who's missed only one game while adding superior defense at third base for a team that is likely to win the division also bodes well for him. This is one race that figures to go down to the last day, with the deciding factor possibly being whether the Astros win the AL West.

As for the AL Cy Young Award, Cam Schlittler , the Yankees ' 25-year-old sophomore, has zoomed ahead of the Blue Jays' Dylan Cease with a season for the ages, including a major league-leading 1.95 ERA and 0.904 WHIP and the most starts in Yankee history allowing one or fewer runs (21). His 1.14 ERA for 16 road starts is also the lowest in American League history.

Over in the National League, with Ohtani shackled with knee and bicep injuries that have prevented him from pitching since July 3, effectively ending his chances for a fourth straight MVP, the Cubs ' 24-year-old Pete Crow-Armstrong has stepped up with a phenomenal breakthrough season. Going into the weekend, Crow-Armstrong, who's played every game, was leading the majors in slugging, OPS and total bases and was second behind Kyle Schwarber in the NL in homers with 44 and third in RBIs with 105. On Aug. 29 he hit three homers in a game and with his 44th homer on Sept. 17 surpassed Hall of Famer Billy Williams as the most by a left-handed hitter in Cubs history.

Sorry, but we're again unable to refrain from reminding that Crow-Armstrong was the Mets ' 2020 first-round draft pick who, the next season, they traded to the Cubs for two months of rental free agent Javy Baez.

When it comes to the Rookies of the Year, I realize in this lost season for the Mets there's been a lot of buzz for Nolan McLean and Carson Benge, but neither are going to win the NL award. That would have to be Cincinnati 's unsung Sal Stewart , who even if nobody probably had him on their Rookie of the Year bingo card at the start of the season, happens to be leading all NL rookies in homers (32) and RBIs (110) and has played every day. An equally strong favorite for the AL Rookie of the Year is Cleveland lefty Parker Messick , a second-round draft pick out of Florida State three years ago, who leads all AL rookies in wins (12), ERA (2.57), strikeouts (186) and WHIP (1.04).

articles.title: West Indies announce squads for India tour: John Campbell returns, Kamil Pooran earns maiden T20I call-up
articles.summary: Cricket News: West Indies have brought back experienced opener John Campbell for their upcoming ODI series against India, while Kamil Pooran has received his first .
articles.body: West Indies have brought back experienced opener John Campbell for their upcoming ODI series against India, while Kamil Pooran has received his first T20I call-up. The Caribbean side will face India in three ODIs and five T20Is from September 27 to October 17, with the series spread across eight cities.Campbell returns after missing the last two ODIs against New Zealand because of a hamstring injury. Captain Shai Hope will lead the 15-member ODI squad, which also includes young batter Jewel Andrew. Andrew replaces Ackeem Auguste, who is still recovering from surgery he underwent in August.Shimron Hetmyer, who featured in West Indies' final two ODIs against New Zealand, has been left out of the ODI squad. However, he will return for the T20I series after being given additional time to recover following the Caribbean Premier League.India series a chance to prepare for World CupThe first two ODIs against India will bring the automatic qualification phase for the 2027 ICC Men's ODI World Cup to an end. West Indies, however, will have to play a qualification tournament early next year after failing to finish ahead of their closest rivals in the standings.Head coach Daren Sammy believes the India series will give his team a valuable chance to test themselves against the world's top-ranked ODI and T20I side and prepare for the World Cup."Playing against the top team in the world presents us with a chance to fine tune and improve our performances as an ODI team which has seen quality performances across the cycle," Sammy said.In the T20I squad, the biggest talking point is the inclusion of Kamil, who has earned his maiden call-up after an impressive recent run. The right-handed opener scored 273 runs in eight innings at a strike rate of 159.64 and an average of 39.Quentin Sampson, who was part of West Indies' T20 World Cup squad earlier this year in India, has also been selected. Experienced all-rounder Jason Holder, meanwhile, has been rested.West Indies ODI squad: Shai Hope (captain), Jewel Andrew, John Campbell, Keacy Carty, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Justin Greaves, Amir Jangoo, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Vitel Lawes, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Sherfane Rutherford, Jayden Seales. West Indies look to build for next T20 World CupThe T20I squad also features Hope, Roston Chase, Hetmyer, Akeal Hosein, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer."We are looking to build on the momentum from our series win against Sri Lanka, with the long-term goal of developing a strong core of players ahead of the next T20 World Cup," Sammy said.The West Indies squad will leave the Caribbean on September 21 and reach Thiruvananthapuram on September 23, four days before the ODI series begins.West Indies T20I squad: Shai Hope (captain), Jewel Andrew, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Shimron Hetmyer, Akeal Hosein, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Kamil Pooran, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Quentin Sampson, Romario Shepherd, Shamar Springer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: East Zone’s new cricketing core: How Bihar and Jharkhand talent powered Duleep Trophy win
articles.summary: Cricket News: When South Zone and East Zone faced-off in the Duleep Trophy final, captain Tilak Varma’s team was widely considered as the favourite. South Zone were.
articles.body: When South Zone and East Zone faced-off in the Duleep Trophy final, captain Tilak Varma’s team was widely considered as the favourite. South Zone were not only playing at home, but had added in-form batter Devdutt Paddikal and Test regular Mohammed Siraj to the playing XI. There was a difference in pedigree too. South Zone were 19-time winners and East Zone had taken home the inter-zonal trophy only twice, the last in 2012-13.But matches are not decided by reputation or history. East outplayed the hosts in every area, including hunger and self-belief to win the trophy. Even the sparse Chennai crowd clapped for the visiting side, especially for captain Ishan Kishan, a reborn cricketer whose monumental 270 first set an uphill task for Varma’s side, and whose feisty 80 shut the door on South’s faint revival hopes in the second.In the 1980s and earlier, East Zone were mostly also-rans in Duleep Trophy. The inter-zonal trophy began in 1961-62, but EZ won its first title only in 2011-12, with Wriddhiman Saha and Shami being the key to that triumph. Next season, Jharkhand’s underappreciated Ishank Jaggi’s ton fashioned East’s repeat success.Now, Jharkhand is a potent force in domestic cricket. In Dec 2025, the mineral-rich state claimed the T20 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy for the first time. Is it any surprise that Kishan scored a ton in the final and was Player of the Match, as in the Duleep Trophy final?Carved out of Bihar, Jharkhand became a separate state in 2000 — a reason why its biggest star, MS Dhoni, began his first-class career playing for (then) Rabri Devi ruled state in 1999. Kishan comes from Bihar, whose cricket association was mired in controversy for years. But several other Jharkhand players, who excelled with the bat in the Duleep final, are born and bred in the fledgling picturesque state. Kumar Kushagra, the 21-year-old ’keeper who stroked to 101 and 46 in the final and is part of the India ‘A’ squad, was born in the steel city of Bokaro. The Dhanbad-born 23-year-old offie Mohammed Kounain Quraishi cruised to 116 in the second innings while claiming the vital wicket of Varma. But Ranchi-born Shikhar Mohan was the stand-out newbie. The 21-year-old southpaw contributed with 85 and 52, displaying calm under pressure in the second innings. He was not only a livewire in the outfield but also stepped in as a left-arm spinner and claimed two wickets when senior Anukul Roy, another Jharkhand-born player, hurt his bowling finger.This was a team triumph. On pitches with different requirements, Bengal pacers Mukesh Kumar and Shami were better than their opposite numbers in both the semis and final. The tournament was a test for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s red-ball credentials. He demonstrated that he can adjust, even dominate. He remains a work in progress, especially against spin. The teenager must be evaluated not only by the runs he scores, but the way he scores them.Irrespective of where they ply their trade, players born in Bihar and Jharkhand are the fulcrum of the new rising East. There was a time when the zonal side was dominated by home-grown Bengal players. articles.title: BCCI to comply with NSG act once cricket is notified as designated sport
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: The BCCI’s position on the National Sports Governance Act dominated discussions at the board’s 95th annual general meeting on Friday, with sec.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The BCCI’s position on the National Sports Governance Act dominated discussions at the board’s 95th annual general meeting on Friday, with secretary Devajit Saikia saying the body would comply with the law once cricket is officially notified as a designated sport.Saikia, however, said the BCCI would not come under the RTI Act because it does not receive govt grants. He said the board pays about Rs 3,000 crore annually in income tax, unlike other national sports federations that receive govt funding. “Regarding the Sports Act, our stand is very clear,” Saikia said after the AGM. “There are a lot of things yet to be done by the concerned authority. Once those exercises are completed, and once BCCI comes under the Sports Act, a notification has to be issued to make cricket a designated sport. Till that time, we are not supposed to do anything.”Saikia said the BCCI would respond to the Supreme Court on Oct 27, when the matter is next listed. “Whenever that notification comes, we will immediately act and do our work as per the rules of the new sports act.” Saikia also argued that cricket should not be treated like other govt-funded sports bodies. “We are paying 3,000 crore in tax annually to the govt. Unlike other sports federations, we don’t take any govt funding. Hence, cricket cannot be treated as a designated sport under the National Sports Governance Act 2025,” he said.BCCI plans centenary celebrations from Dec 2027The BCCI will complete 100 years in Dec 2028 and plans to form a committee for year-long centenary celebrations beginning in Dec 2027. Saikia said the board also discussed plans to mark the 20th edition of the IPL next year.“In Dec 2028, we will complete 100 years of the BCCI, so we will hold centenary celebrations from Dec 2027 for one year,” he said. “The IPL, which will start from March-end next year, will have its 20th edition. We have discussed that it should be done in a grand way.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Vaibhav Sooryavanshi can't transition to Test cricket': Ex-cricketer says 'he doesn't have the technique'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may still be only 15, but the sheer impact of his performances has already led to questions about whether he can eventually conqu.
articles.body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may still be only 15, but the sheer impact of his performances has already led to questions about whether he can eventually conquer all three formats. The Samastipur-born left-hander has made a stunning start to his career, with his exploits in the IPL and at the international level putting him firmly under the spotlight.His immediate future, however, remains in T20 cricket. Sooryavanshi did not feature in any of the matches, with Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma preferred at the top of the order. Given the team's desire to maintain continuity, the decision was understandable despite the teenager's impressive IPL campaign.The discussion has now moved beyond the teenager's place in India's T20I XI, with his potential in Test cricket becoming another talking point. Sooryavanshi has limited red-ball experience and is nowhere close to a Test call-up at present, but former England spinner Monty Panesar has already offered his assessment of whether the youngster can make the transition to the longest format.Speaking on the Beyond23 Cricket Podcast alongside former Australia captain Michael Clarke, Panesar questioned whether Sooryavanshi possesses the technique required to succeed in Test cricket.“I can’t see Sooryavanshi transitioning to Test cricket. Harry Brook is the only one right now who’s in the top 10 in Tests and T20Is. But I just don’t think Sooryavanshi has got the technique," Panesar said.Clarke, however, offered a contrasting view. The former Australia captain argued that players can succeed across all three formats if they have the necessary skill and talent, pointing to Virat Kohli and AB de Villiers as examples.“I think you can still play all three formats. Virat Kohli and AB de Villiers showed that. These guys were brilliant Test cricketers and unbelievable T20 cricketers as well. If a player from this generation, like Sooryavanshi, can make the transition into Test cricket, it is going to be unreal to watch," said Clarke.Clarke also highlighted Sooryavanshi's power and exceptional ability to read the ball as his biggest strengths at this stage of his career. He believes the technical aspects of the youngster's batting can develop with greater exposure to different conditions.“Right now, power is still his main thing, and he has an amazing eye. He picks the ball as well as any young cricketer in the world. The technique will get better the more he tours with India and trains in different conditions," said Sooryavanshi.Clarke went a step further in backing the teenager's long-term potential, suggesting he has the talent to become a star across formats if he chooses to pursue that route."He’s talented enough that, if he wants to do it, I can’t see any reason why he can’t be a superstar in all three formats," he added.Sooryavanshi has already had some exposure to red-ball cricket. articles.title: Stephen Fleming: England Test coach on Bazball, Ben Stokes, team discipline and more
articles.summary: Read what England's new Test coach Stephen Fleming had to say about Bazball, Ben Stokes, the team's discipline issues and his own philosophy.
articles.body:
Stephen Fleming has given his first interviews since becoming England's Test coach.

The New Zealander, who replaces his close friend Brendon McCullum, spoke at length - covering Bazball, Ben Stokes' departure, England's discipline problems, his own coaching style and more.

Fleming on Carse and England's discipline problems

England have been dogged by off-field issues in recent times. Harry Brook was involved in an altercation with a nightclub bouncer last year, Ben Duckett was videoed apparently drunk in Australia, Stokes and Gus Atkinson broke a team curfew and Brydon Carse was investigated by police after an incident in Derby.

Fleming said: "It's been disappointing, because I understand what people are working towards. These events can derail a lot of things and divert attention from what really matters.

"When I look at epitomising an international cricketer and what they should stand for, it's Joe [Root].

"When he sits in an interview and openly expresses his disappointment, or uses "hacked off", I know there's work to be done.

"Also, the belonging, identity, what are we doing here together and how we can be the best version of ourselves. A lot of that work has begun.

"That's one of the key things for me to develop and my work with Joe has begun."

On Carse, specifically, Fleming said the bowler is available for selection but added: "There are standards. We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set."

Fleming has a long-standing relationship with McCullum as a former team-mate, friend and business partner. He replaces his fellow Black Cap, whose tenure as Test coach began with stunning highs before turning sour with the Ashes defeat and his sacking this summer.

"He was heart-sore it had worked out that way, but he was incredibly positive about the experience and opportunity.

"He's been unwavering on that. His belief about where these teams can go is strong, and that was a major part when I was talking to him about doing the role.

"I love his confidence and aggressive nature. I'm more measured.

"Somewhere in between we've got a beautiful working relationship with a huge amount of respect.

"I have so much respect for what Ben Stokes and Brendon did for this English side. They changed the landscape of cricket and that's a really powerful thing."

McCullum's side beat New Zealand and South Africa in their first summer before a memorable win in Pakistan. They were unable to win any of their five-Test series against India and Australia, however.

"I was in awe of what that team were doing and how they were doing it.

"The last 12 months, the evolution – teams caught up, there was talent lost, a lot of reasons. That's now my opportunity.

"There was a thousand wickets lost – [James] Anderson, [Stuart] Broad, then [Chris] Woakes.

"When you do something special and you start doing it differently, everybody else takes a bit of time, then they catch up.

"The pressure then goes on to evolution and that can create some challenges. That's my take on it.

"The Ashes wasn't what they wanted and that is what this team is measured on.

"All I can think about is now my opportunity to pick it up, and maybe add my style, which is looking at personality, a little bit more measured."

Stokes, who announced his shock retirement in June, played under Fleming at Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League. Fleming revealed the pair spoke at Durham earlier this week.

Fleming said: "He'd just come off another monster bowling spell.

"He was in a great space, really happy, enjoying his time with Durham.

"He's got a good winter planned with the family and is very much at peace with his decision. When a player makes that decision to retire, I respect that decision 100%.

"To try to turn that around and question that is wrong. I know how much goes into that type of decision, and I respect that."

Fleming was named England coach on 30 July but did not take charge of the recent series win over Pakistan, instead following from home.

Fleming said: "There were commitments and family commitments I had that I just wasn't in a position to break. That's more about me as a person, than dropping everything and coming over here.

"I watched and connected with Joe and the team straight away once it was approved – I've got a stress fracture in my left ear from phone calls.

"Watching remotely, I won't say it was an advantage, but watching them operate with eyes wide open as to what was expected, the opportunity, the challenges, and there was also another part – introducing Joe back into captaincy, and Marcus Trescothick the opportunity to do the head coach's role.

"That's part of why I love the game, bringing people forward, developing people, leadership, and they did brilliantly.

"It gave me an opportunity to catch my breath, and then start pretty fresh with a clear mind about what's ahead."

Though Fleming has extensive experience in franchise cricket, he has never coached a red-ball side. He was New Zealand captain for 80 of his 111 Tests, however.

On the playing style he wants, Fleming said: "If people were watching a team, I'd love people to say they are well-planned, there's a discipline and a really strong basic structure to what we're doing, but there's also a bit of flair.

"That's not necessarily me and the way I played, but it's what I loved about this English side when they started playing like this.

"It's taking the best of that and adding that planning aspect, so if supporters could look at us and say 'yeah, they are disciplined, well-planned and competitive'. That's a good start.

"The greatest thing for a team to do is to be able to play conditions and situations.

"One thing this team has earned is the ability to be positive. One of the other aspects is winning the tough moments and making sure we don't just play entertaining cricket and win moments, but win games."

On the Ashes and the World Test Championship

Fleming's first series in charge is against South Africa in December. After two Tests in Bangladesh and a one-off anniversary Test in Melbourne in the winter, attention will then turn to next summer's Ashes. Fleming rejected the idea English cricket is too obsessed by beating Australia.

"No, because I have an obsession with it as well," he said. "New Zealand has an obsession with it, we love it.

"We want to beat Aussie. We're heavily linked to England performances. We have a deep desire to beat Australia in everything, as the little cousin.

"We are linked, and I'm incredibly excited about being part of it. You don't think you're ever going to get that opportunity.

"To have that opportunity and be part of it, I can't wait. I want to be my best self and have a team that represents itself in the best possible way. I've got a vision of that and it's aspirational. It will be brilliant."

On the World Test Championship, an event England are yet to reach the final of, he said: "England could do much better than that.

"And even attitude just around the over rate, I think, comes down to identity and style of play.

"And if that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it along with every other marquee event that comes our way?"

articles.title: Stephen Fleming: New England coach arrives with desire to 'beat the Aussies'
articles.summary: New Test coach Stephen Fleming says he shares English cricket’s “obsession” with the Ashes and arrives with the goal to “beat the Aussies”.
articles.body:
New Test coach Stephen Fleming said he shared English cricket's "obsession" with the Ashes and arrives with the goal to "beat the Aussies".

Fleming was speaking to the media for the first time since being appointed in July and ahead of taking charge for the tour of South Africa in December.

Like his predecessor Brendon McCullum, Fleming is from New Zealand, the "little cousin" to Australia, in his words.

The next Ashes series is in the UK next summer, when England will look to defeat the Australians for the first time since 2015 and avenge a dismal 4-1 defeat down under last winter.

Asked if England are too obsessed with beating Australia, Fleming told BBC Sport: "No, because I have an obsession with it as well. New Zealand has an obsession with it, we love it.

"We want to beat the Aussies. We're heavily linked to England performances. We have a deep desire to beat Australia in everything, as the little cousin. We are linked, and I'm incredibly excited about being part of it.

"You don't think you're ever going to get that opportunity. To have that opportunity and be part of it, I can't wait.

"I want to be my best self and have a team that represents itself in the best possible way. I've got a vision of that and it's aspirational. It will be brilliant."

Listen to the full Stephen Fleming interview on the TMS podcast

Fleming on England discipline, Stokes, late arrival and coaching styles

Fleming, the former New Zealand captain, did not taste victory in any of the 14 Tests he played against Australia.

He succeeds his former team-mate McCullum, who was sacked as Test coach earlier this summer, but remains as boss of the white-ball team. England won only two of McCullum's final 10 Tests in charge, including the hammering in Australia.

Part of the criticism of England under McCullum and former captain Ben Stokes was their inability to adapt to the changing situations of Test cricket, as well as a lack of attention to detail.

Fleming is a great friend of McCullum – the pair are business partners. He described the difference between the two as being: "I'll bet on the favourite and he'll bet on the longest odds possible."

On whether a Test team should have a brand or style, Fleming said: "I don't think so. The greatest thing for a team to do is to be able to play conditions and situations.

"I'd love people to say we are well-planned, there's a discipline and a really strong basic structure to what we're doing, but there's also a bit of flair."

The final months of McCullum's reign were dogged by late-night drinking controversies, which continued after England changed the Test coach.

Though Carse will face no action from the police, he now faces an investigation from the Cricket Regulator.

He remains available for England selection, albeit has not been part of a squad in any format since the Derby incident.

"There are standards," said Fleming. "We pick on runs and wickets primarily, but I think it's foolish not to also say there are standards that need to be set.

"You need to behave in accordance with your position. We're in a very privileged position, and it's understanding that privilege and what goes along with it. It can't be convenient. You can't be when it suits you to do the right things, then when you don't want it to suit you, not.

"You've got to live it every day. If we can create something when you want to live it every day and better, then that's really powerful."

Fleming was at Old Trafford for England's defeat of Sri Lanka in the third T20 on Saturday. Earlier in the week he visited a number of counties and met Stokes during Durham's draw against Worcestershire.

Stokes abruptly retired from international cricket in July and has a previous relationship with Fleming from their time together with Chennai Super Kings at the Indian Premier League.

But Fleming said he had too much "respect" for Stokes' decision to attempt to coax him out of retirement.

"He was in a great space, really happy, enjoying his time with Durham," said Fleming.

"He's got a good winter planned with the family and is very much at peace with his decision. When a player makes that decision to retire, I respect that decision 100%.

"To try to turn that around and question that is wrong. I know how much goes into that type of decision, and I respect that."

'Flemball is a medical condition' - analysis

Almost two months after being appointed Test coach, Stephen Fleming outlined what the England team may look like under his stewardship.

He was calm, measured and authoritative, perhaps showing he is exactly the sort of leader England need after a chaotic period on and off the pitch.

There were also signs of Fleming's character and sense of humour. He joked he has a "stress fracture of the left ear" after all the phone calls he has had with those connected with the England team, then laughed about occasionally turning up in fancy dress to relax the environment of his Chennai Super Kings team.

Most revealing was the description of his relationship with Brendon McCullum – "I'll bet on the favourite and he'll bet on the longest odds possible". There were plenty of times during McCullum's reign as Test coach where those long-odds bets were placed, while Fleming seems much more likely to play the percentages.

The two are great friends, which should help with a split-coaching dynamic that has not always served England well in the past. "Big brother" was one way the Fleming-McCullum dynamic was referred to, and there was a sense that England now have a grown-up in charge, following the freewheeling of McCullum.

Fleming covered a range of topics: he won't try to persuade Ben Stokes to come out of retirement, he will give the World Test Championship a level of respect lacking from previous England teams, he explained he missed the Pakistan series because of family and commercial commitments.

Fleming also addressed discipline and the late-night controversies that have dogged England in the past 12 months. Talk of "standards" may not be good news for Brydon Carse's prospects of a swift return to the set-up.

And, of course, there was the question of "Flemball", dismissed as a "medical condition".

On this evidence, Fleming's England will be more assured, mature and level than the team led by McCullum. Possibly less fun, too.

The most important thing is they win more, starting in South Africa in December.

articles.title: Stephen Fleming: England's new head coach targets No 1 spot in Test rankings but says 'work to be done' on discipline
articles.summary: Stephen Fleming says he has had "a lot of contact" with Test captain Joe Root during the Pakistan series and has spoken with former skipper Ben Stokes following his international retirement earlier this summer; "Ben's happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision", he said
articles.body:
In June, Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended from the second Test of the 2-1 series loss to New Zealand due to a nightclub incident that occurred in the wake of their opening win at Lord's.

Last month, Brydon Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series whitewash of Pakistan, prompting Test captain Joe Root to describe himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

Carse did not face any charges after police closed their investigation.

"It's disappointing," Fleming said. "The way that players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me."

He added: "I watched Joe in the press conference, and when he voices his displeasure at the behaviour, I think that said it all.

"If you want a great example of how to behave as an international cricketer, Joe Root is it.

"There's work to be done, and that comes back to making sure we're tying into something a bit bigger than oneself."

As well as having "a lot of contact" with Root since accepting the Test job on July 30 and throughout the Pakistan series - which Fleming was not yet in post for, due to family and commercial commitments - the new coach said he had also been in touch with Stokes, who retired from international cricket in June.

Amid suggestions of a possible return for the home Ashes series next summer, Fleming said of the 35-year-old: "He's really happy and seemed to be really at peace with his decision.

"My view is that when a player decides to retire, it's a big decision, and I have the utmost respect for that decision."

Fleming excited for Ashes and keen to take England to top

Fleming admitted he is already excited about coaching England in next summer's Ashes, calling it "an absolute highlight", while he also talked up the potential of the team he is about to take over.

"I would love to be in charge of the number one Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration," Fleming said.

"My honest appraisal is it's a great time to be the head coach. I think it's a real opportunity with the players that are coming through.

"The fast bowlers as an example, I loved watching them operate in the [Pakistan] Test series recently.

"Also, the introduction of [Jordan] Cox and [Dan] Lawrence was nice, when you've got someone like [Jacob] Bethell [to come back].

"There's talent there competing for places, and that's always the barometer. If you're leaving very good players out, then you're going to be in a healthy situation."

Fleming added on the World Test Championship, in which England sit sixth in the 2025-2027 cycle - having failed to reach the final of any of the previous three editions: "I think England could do much better in that.

"If that's one of the pinnacle trophies in world cricket, why would we not be trying to get it, along with every other marquee event that comes our way?

"That opportunity is real, but there's a huge amount of work to do."

Fleming rejects 'Flemball' in pursuit of 'cricket sense'

As for the playing style Fleming will look for his team to adopt, he was keen to praise the prior work of Stokes and former New Zealand team-mate - England's current white-ball coach - Brendon McCullum, but said he is looking to "combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments".

There will be no 'Bazball' style moniker to accompany his team's style, however, as per his predecessor.

"That's a medical condition," Fleming joked when presented with the prospect of 'Flemball'.

"The way they [Stokes and McCullum] changed the nature of Test cricket was quite remarkable, and I have a huge amount of respect for the courage that that took.

"Obviously, the last 12 months it hasn't evolved as they would have liked and the fans would have liked, but I still acknowledge that period of two years [prior]."

He added: "I really loved the positive play and the freeing up of the England players, so if I could take that and combine a little bit of cricket sense around some key moments.

"There are key times in a match that you have to be really smart, and maybe we can just work a bit harder on that - but still combine positive nature of the players that are in there."

Root is 'greatness' and 'the best guy to captain Test team'

Talking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast , Fleming elaborated further on the respect he has for Root and how delighted he is to have him as captain of the Test team.

Root had previously captained England from 2017-2022 before being replaced by Stokes following a barren run of one win in his last 17 Tests.

Upon Stokes' resignation, white-ball skipper Harry Brook could have been an all-format option, but Fleming is thrilled that Root accepted the role again.

"I am a really big fan of Root," Fleming said. "I think he is a wonderful player and ambassador for the game, so to work with him was really appealing.

"I just knew that he is the best guy to captain this side. He epitomises everything that is great about an international player. He is greatness, but a wonderful human being in the way that he conducts himself and can go about being great.

"He is such a great role model and such a perfect person for a young group of players. It was a no-brainer, for me, for him to be captain.

"Root is in charge. If he is going out and making key decisions, he is in charge. My role is very closely linked to provide him with what he needs. That can be criticism, constructively, so it's not just a yes position.

"I want him to be the best he can be and I think there is still room to grow in his captaincy with this group. I don't necessarily know what that looks like but I know there is growth and that's exciting."

articles.title: Shafali Verma’s century and India’s bowling blitz crush Bangladesh as defending champions storm into Asian Games final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Defending champions India Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 with a commanding 114-run victory over Banglade.
articles.body: Defending champions India Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 with a commanding 114-run victory over Bangladesh in the semi-final at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan.After posting a formidable 195/4 in 20 overs, India’s bowlers dismantled Bangladesh’s chase, bowling them out for just 81 in 15.4 overs. The emphatic win guarantees India a medal and sets up a gold-medal clash against Sri Lanka on September 22.Shafali’s historic century powers India to 195India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat, and the top order made the most of the decision. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma provided a blistering start, racing to 71 in the powerplay. Mandhana struck 37 off 18 balls before falling, but not before becoming the leading run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket and the first Indian woman to reach 100 sixes in the format.Shafali then took charge, producing a sensational 100 off 49 deliveries, including nine sixes and three fours. She became the first player to score a century in women’s cricket at the Asian Games. Harmanpreet added a valuable 40 off 33 balls as India finished on 195/4, setting Bangladesh a target of 196.India bowlers crush Bangladesh’s chaseBangladesh’s reply quickly unravelled as they slipped to 9/2 early in the innings. India’s bowlers maintained the pressure, taking wickets at regular intervals and leaving the visitors unable to build a partnership. Dilara Akter offered some resistance with 27 off 23 balls, but the rest of the batting line-up struggled, with eight batters dismissed for single-digit scores.Nandani Sharma and Deepti Sharma led India’s attack with three wickets each. Nandani finished with 3/25, while Deepti returned an economical 3/7. Shree Charani also made an impact with 2/7 as Bangladesh were dismissed for 81 in 15.4 overs.India set up gold-medal clash against Sri LankaThe victory sends India into the gold-medal match, where they will face Sri Lanka on Tuesday, September 22. Sri Lanka booked their place in the final after defeating Pakistan by eight wickets in the first semi-final.India will now look to defend the gold medal they won at the 2022 Asian Games, while Pakistan and Bangladesh will meet in the bronze-medal playoff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: England’s recent Test victory over Pakistan has offered a timely boost as the team prepares for a new chapter under incoming head coach Stephen Flemin.
articles.body: England’s recent Test victory over Pakistan has offered a timely boost as the team prepares for a new chapter under incoming head coach Stephen Fleming. But the former New Zealand captain has set his sights on a much bigger goal: taking England back to the top of the Test rankings and making the World Test Championship a central part of the team’s ambitions.Fleming addressed the media for the first time since being appointed England’s Test coach, describing the role as one of cricket’s most prestigious. He has signed a contract with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) until September 2030, following a two-week recruitment process.“I would love to be in charge of the No. 1 Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration,” Fleming said, referring to England’s bid to reclaim the top spot for the first time since 2012.His first assignment will be a winter series against South Africa, followed by a home Ashes campaign, an occasion he said he has long admired as a New Zealander.Building an identity and targeting major honoursFleming said he has already begun working with Test captain Joe Root, with an emphasis on shaping England’s identity and building a strong sense of belonging within the squad.“The way players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me,” he said, adding that the team’s style of play would be shaped more by the players themselves.The World Test Championship is also high on Fleming’s agenda. England have yet to reach the final in any of the competition’s first three editions.“England could do much better than that,” he said, describing the WTC as an aspirational target alongside other major events. Fleming added that improving the team’s approach, including its over-rate, would be part of developing a clearer identity.Fleming takes over after McCullum eraFleming succeeds Brendon McCullum, who had been in charge since 2022. England’s recent struggles over the past 18 months have formed part of the backdrop to the coaching change, though Fleming said he sees an opportunity to move the team forward.He said McCullum had been honest about the team’s situation and believed there was still potential within the group."That was one thing that will probably hurt him (McCullum) a little bit (underperformance) - I think he feels what I feel now, that there's an opportunity around the corner. He was also realistic about what had gone on and just very honest. It's interesting when you go to watch as a bystander for the first half of the year, then things change quite quickly to a real narrow focus on where the team was at,'' he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Stephen Fleming: Stuart Broad excited at what new England Test cricket coach can do for Joe Root's captaincy
articles.summary: Sky Sports pundit Stuart Broad on Stephen Fleming-Joe Root relationship: "Where Joe needs a bit of help with his captaincy is taking a bit of weight off his shoulders at times, allowing him to concentrate on batting, make tactical decisions and get feedback throughout to help England out"
articles.body:
Fleming was named as countryman Brendon McCullum's successor in late July but did not lead the side for the recent 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to family commitments.

The 53-year-old recently flew to England for a short trip to chat with ECB officials and Test skipper Root as well as the counties, and was with the national team as they completed a 3-0 T20I whitewash under white-ball coach McCullum in Manchester on Saturday .

Fleming - who has never been a head coach in red-ball cricket before but has extensive franchise-league experience, chiefly with Chennai Super Kings in the IPL - spoke to media ahead of the final T20I, including to Michael Atherton for the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast.

Broad said after listening to former New Zealand captain Fleming's chat with Atherton, in which he lauded Root: "What struck me was his love of leadership.

"He spoke a lot about that and strategy rather than really intricate coaching, so I am assuming he will pass a lot of the technique coaching on to his bowling coach, batting coach etc, which is what they are there to do.

'Root needs feedback Fleming will give him'

"I think what excites me is him working with Root's captaincy.

"Fleming was a good captain and has worked a lot with MS Dhoni at Chennai. He has learnt about tactical stuff on the field and how to manage changing rooms as well.

"Where Joe needs, or would like, a bit of help with his captaincy is taking a bit of weight off his shoulders at times, allowing him to just concentrate on his batting, make some tactical decisions and get feedback throughout the game to help England out.

"Joe hasn't naturally got a bowling attack that will feed back a lot of tactical advice so I think he needs that.

"As a coach you are very reliant on your captain. Fleming has had a very good one in Dhoni and maybe not quite clicked with others he tried to have success with.

"But the way he talked about Root, I imagine he will click with him."

Broad does not view this being Fleming's first red-ball head coach role as an issue.

"He loved playing the game, he loves studying and coaching the game, so you love all formats," said the former England seamer.

"He made his name in Test match cricket and I have no doubt he has watched and been around current players."

'England need leaders to start winning Test series'

When Ben Stokes quit internationals at the end of the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer, there were few options to replace him as captain besides Root - who first led England between 2017 and 2022 - and white-ball skipper Harry Brook.

Broad says a key part of Fleming's remit is to develop more leaders as England look to return to the peak of Test cricket, having not won any of the four five-match series they played against either Australia or India in the Bazball era.

The pundit added: "Fleming has a group that is exciting but England have also lost a lot of cricket over the last 18 months, so he has some moulding to do.

"A big problem for this team has been the lack of leaders and you can see it on the field.

"I don't really mind a lack of leaders to choose as captain when you have Root and Brook as options but on the field there has been a stark problem.

"Fleming has noticed that and will focus on that. He will drop nuggets of information in consistently throughout to try and build leadership. We need leaders to start winning Test series."
